title.zh: 卷二百零七 列傳第一百三十二 宦者上
title.raw: 卷二百零七 列傳第一百三十二 宦者上 Volume 207 Biographies 132: Imperial Officials 1

sentences.zh: 宦者上

translations.literal: Eunuchs, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs, Part One

sentences.zh: 唐制：內侍省官有內侍四，內常侍六，內謁者監、內給事各十，謁者十二，典引十八，寺伯、寺人各六。

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations, the Palace Attendants Office had four inner attendants, six inner vice attendants, ten each for inner usher supervisors and inner provisioners, twelve ushers, eighteen protocol guides, and six each for temple stewards and temple servants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, the Palace Attendants Office comprised four inner attendants, six inner vice attendants, ten inner usher supervisors and ten inner provisioners, twelve ushers, eighteen protocol guides, and six temple stewards and six temple servants apiece.

sentences.zh: 又有五局：一曰掖廷，主宮嬪簿最；

translations.literal: There were also five bureaus: the first was called Yeting, in charge of palace women's registers;
translations.idiomatic: There were also five bureaus: the first, Yeting, kept the registers of palace women;

sentences.zh: 二曰宮闈，扈門闌；

translations.literal: the second was Gongwei, guarding gates and thresholds;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Gongwei, guarded gates and thresholds;

sentences.zh: 三曰奚官，治宮中疾病死喪；

translations.literal: the third was Xiguan, managing illness, death, and mourning within the palace;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Xiguan, handled sickness, death, and mourning in the palace;

sentences.zh: 四曰內僕，主供帳燈燭；

translations.literal: the fourth was Neipu, in charge of supplying curtains, lamps, and candles;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, Neipu, supplied curtains, lamps, and candles;

sentences.zh: 五曰內府，主中藏給納。

translations.literal: the fifth was Neifu, in charge of the inner treasury's receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth, Neifu, managed receipts and disbursements from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 局有令，有丞，皆宦者為之。

translations.literal: Each bureau had a director and an assistant director, all of whom were eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau had a director and a deputy, and eunuchs filled every such post.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔內侍省不立三品官，以內侍為之長，階第四，不任以事，惟門閣守禦、廷內掃除、稟食而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong decreed that the Palace Attendants Office should not establish third-rank posts; the inner attendant served as its head at the fourth rank, entrusted with no affairs of state—only guarding gates and passes, sweeping within the court, and distributing food.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered that the Palace Attendants Office appoint no third-rank officers. The inner attendant ranked fourth and held no public duties beyond guarding gates, sweeping the inner court, and issuing rations.

sentences.zh: 武後時，稍增其人。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, their numbers were gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu their numbers were gradually increased.

sentences.zh: 至中宗，黃衣乃二千員，七品以上員外置千員，然衣朱紫者尚少。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Zhongzong, those in yellow robes numbered two thousand, with an additional thousand seventh-rank and above placed outside the quota, yet those wearing scarlet and purple were still few.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Zhongzong's reign, eunuchs in yellow robes numbered two thousand, with another thousand seventh-rank and above beyond the quota, though those in scarlet and purple remained few.

sentences.zh: 玄宗承平，財用富足，誌大事奢，不愛惜賞賜爵位。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong enjoyed prolonged peace, revenues were ample, his ambitions were grand and his tastes lavish, and he did not stint with rewards, gifts, or ennoblements.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzong's long peace the treasury swelled; his ambitions ran grand and his tastes lavish, and he lavished rewards, gifts, and titles without restraint.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶中，宮嬪大率至四萬，宦官黃衣以上三千員，衣朱紫千餘人。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, palace women generally reached forty thousand; eunuchs in yellow robes and above numbered three thousand, and those in scarlet and purple exceeded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao, palace women numbered roughly forty thousand; eunuchs from yellow-robed rank upward reached three thousand, and more than a thousand wore scarlet or purple.

sentences.zh: 其稱旨者輒拜三品將軍，列戟於門。

translations.literal: Those who pleased him were at once appointed third-rank generals, with halberds arrayed at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: Those who won his favor were promptly made third-rank generals, with halberds displayed at their gates.

sentences.zh: 其在殿頭供奉，委任華重，持節傳命，光焰殷殷動四方。

translations.literal: Those who served at the head of the hall received weighty commissions; bearing credentials they transmitted orders, and their brilliance and authority stirred all four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Those who served at the front of the hall carried heavy responsibility; bearing imperial credentials they relayed orders, and their splendor and power shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 所至郡縣奔走，獻遺至萬計。

translations.literal: Wherever they went, commanderies and counties rushed about; gifts presented reached into the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they traveled, prefectures and counties scrambled to serve them, and tribute offered ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 修功德，市禽鳥，一為之使，猶且數千緡。

translations.literal: For merit-building projects or purchasing birds and beasts, a single commission as their agent still cost several thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: A single errand to fund merit works or buy birds and beasts still cost thousands of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 監軍持權，節度返出其下。

translations.literal: Army supervisors held power, and military commissioners in turn fell beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisors wielded real power, and even military commissioners ranked below them.

sentences.zh: 於是甲舍、名園、上腴之田為中人所名者半京畿矣。

translations.literal: Thus mansions, famous gardens, and the richest fields claimed by eunuchs made up half the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Mansions, celebrated gardens, and the finest farmland claimed by eunuchs came to fill half the capital region.

sentences.zh: 肅、代庸弱，倚為扞衛，故輔國以尚父顯，元振以援立奮，朝恩以軍容重，然猶未得常主兵也。

translations.literal: Suzong and Daizong were feeble rulers who relied on them as guards; thus Fuguo rose to prominence as Sire Father, Yuanzhen flourished by aiding the enthronement, and Chaoen grew weighty through army supervision—yet they still did not regularly command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong and Daizong were weak sovereigns who leaned on eunuchs as protectors. Fuguo rose as Sire Father, Yuanzhen through aiding the succession, Chaoen through army supervision—yet eunuchs still did not routinely command armies.

sentences.zh: 德宗懲艾泚賊，故以左右神策、天威等軍委宦者主之，置護軍中尉、中護軍，分提禁兵，是以威柄下遷，政在宦人，舉手伸縮，便有輕重。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, chastened by the Zhu Ci rebellion, therefore entrusted the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies, the Heavenly Might Army, and the like to eunuch command; he established the Protector Army Central Commanders and Central Army Protectors to divide control of the palace guards. Thus authority shifted downward, government rested with eunuchs, and a gesture of hand or foot could tip the scales.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by Zhu Ci's rebellion, Dezong placed the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies, the Heavenly Might Army, and others under eunuch command, appointing Protector Army Central Commanders and Central Army Protectors to divide the palace guards. Power sank to the eunuchs; a lifted hand or a glance could decide fortunes.

sentences.zh: 至慓士奇材，則養以為子；

translations.literal: When they met fierce and exceptional talent, they adopted it as sons;
translations.idiomatic: When they encountered fierce, exceptional men, they adopted them as sons;

sentences.zh: 巨鎮強藩，則爭出我門。

translations.literal: great garrisons and powerful provinces vied to claim descent from their households.
translations.idiomatic: great garrisons and powerful provinces competed to trace their rise through eunuch patronage.

sentences.zh: 小人之情，猥險無顧藉，又日夕侍天子，狎則無威，習則不疑，故昏君蔽於所昵，英主禍生所忽。

translations.literal: The nature of petty men is base, treacherous, and without scruple; moreover they attend the Son of Heaven day and night—familiarity erodes awe, habit breeds trust without doubt. Thus muddle-headed rulers are blinded by those they favor, and even sagely rulers meet disaster in what they overlook.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are base, treacherous, and without scruple. Attending the emperor day and night, they wear away awe through familiarity and breed unquestioning trust through habit. Dull rulers are blinded by favorites; even capable rulers are undone by what they overlook.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以遷崩，憲、敬以弒殞，文以憂僨，至昭而天下亡矣。

translations.literal: Xuanzong died in exile; Xianzong and Jingzong perished by assassination; Wenzong died of grief and rage; by Zhaozong the realm was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong died in exile; Xianzong and Jingzong were assassinated; Wenzong died of grief and rage; by Zhaozong the empire was gone.

sentences.zh: 禍始開元，極於天祐，兇愎參會，黨類殲滅，王室從而潰喪，譬猶灼火攻蠹，蠹盡木焚，詎不哀哉！

translations.literal: Disaster began in Kaiyuan and reached its extreme in Tianyou; cruelty and obstinacy converged, factions were annihilated, and the royal house collapsed in turn—like applying fire to burn out worms: when the worms are gone the wood is consumed. How pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Disaster began in Kaiyuan and peaked in Tianyou. Cruelty and obstinacy converged, factions were wiped out, and the royal house collapsed—like burning worms out of wood: when the worms die, the timber is ash. How pitiful!

sentences.zh: 跡其殘氣不剛，柔情易遷，褻則無上，怖則生怨，借之權則專，為禍則迫而近，緩相攻，急相一，此小人常勢也。

translations.literal: Tracing their pattern: their vital force is weak and not firm, their tender feelings shift easily; when treated familiarly they show no deference to superiors, when frightened they breed resentment; lend them power and they monopolize it; when they bring harm it presses close; in slack times they attack one another, in urgent times they unite—such is the constant tendency of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Their pattern runs thus: vital force weak and unsteady, affections quick to shift; treated familiarly they lose all deference, frightened they nurse resentment; given power they monopolize it; when they harm, harm is close at hand; in slack times they turn on one another, in crisis they unite—such is the constant way of petty men.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 梟狐不神，天與之昏，末如亂何。

translations.literal: Owls and foxes are not numinous—Heaven has given them a benighted age; in the end, what can be done about disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Owls and foxes hold no numinous power—Heaven has granted them a benighted age. In the end, what remedy is there for chaos?

sentences.zh: 故取中葉以來宦人之大者稡之篇。

translations.literal: Therefore the great eunuchs from the mid-dynasty onward are gathered in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, this chapter gathers the leading eunuchs from the mid-dynasty onward.

sentences.zh: 楊思勖，羅州石城人，本蘇氏，冒所養姓。

translations.literal: Yang Sixu was a native of Shicheng in Luozhou; his original surname was Su, and he took the surname of his adoptive family.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixu came from Shicheng in Luozhou. His birth surname was Su; he took the surname of the family that raised him.

sentences.zh: 少給事內侍省，從玄宗討內難，擢左監門衛將軍，帝倚為爪牙。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the Palace Attendants Office; he followed Emperor Xuanzong in suppressing the inner turmoil and was promoted to Left Gate Guard general. The emperor relied on him as a personal enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served in the Palace Attendants Office. He followed Xuanzong through the inner turmoil and was raised to Left Gate Guard general. The emperor relied on him as a trusted enforcer.

sentences.zh: 開元初，安南蠻渠梅叔鸞叛，號黑帝，舉三十二州之眾，外結林邑、真臘、金鄰等國，據海南，眾號四十萬。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, the Annan tribal chieftain Mei Shuluan rebelled, styled himself Black Emperor, raised the people of thirty-two prefectures, allied abroad with Linyi, Zhenla, Jinlin, and other states, seized Hainan, and claimed four hundred thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan the Annan chieftain Mei Shuluan rebelled, calling himself the Black Emperor. He rallied thirty-two prefectures, allied with Linyi, Zhenla, Jinlin, and others abroad, seized Hainan, and claimed four hundred thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 思勖請行，詔募首領子弟十萬，與安南大都護光楚客繇馬援故道出不意，賊驢眙不暇謀，遂大敗，封屍為京觀而還。

translations.literal: Sixu asked to go; the court recruited one hundred thousand sons of tribal leaders and, with An-nan Grand Protector Guang Chuke, advanced by Ma Yuan's old route to take the enemy unawares. The rebels stared stupefied without time to plan, were utterly defeated, and he returned after sealing the corpses into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Sixu volunteered. The court raised one hundred thousand sons of tribal leaders and, with An-nan Grand Protector Guang Chuke, marched by Ma Yuan's old route to strike by surprise. The rebels stood stunned with no time to plan, suffered a crushing defeat, and he returned after piling the dead into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 十二年，五溪首領覃行章亂，詔思勖為黔中招討使，率兵六萬往，執行章，斬首三萬級，以功進輔國大將軍，給祿俸、防閣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Wuxi chieftain Qin Xingzhang rebelled. Sixu was appointed Qianzhong pacification commissioner, led sixty thousand troops, captured Xingzhang, and beheaded thirty thousand. For his merit he was advanced to Defender-in-Chief of the State and granted salary and household guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Wuxi chieftain Qin Xingzhang rebelled. Sixu was made Qianzhong pacification commissioner, led sixty thousand men, seized Xingzhang, and took thirty thousand heads. For this he was promoted to Defender-in-Chief of the State with salary and household guards.

sentences.zh: 從封泰山，進驃騎大將軍，封虢國公。

translations.literal: He accompanied the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai, was advanced to Cavalry-in-Chief General, and enfeoffed as Duke of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai, rose to Cavalry-in-Chief General, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guo.

sentences.zh: 邕州封陵獠梁大海反，破賓、橫等州，思勖又平之，禽大海等三千人，討斬支黨皆盡。

translations.literal: In Yongzhou the Fengling Liao chieftain Liang Dahai rebelled and overran Bin, Heng, and other prefectures. Sixu pacified them again, captured Dahai and three thousand others, and hunted down and executed all their partisans.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzhou the Fengling Liao chieftain Liang Dahai rebelled and ravaged Bin, Heng, and other prefectures. Sixu put the rising down again, seized Dahai and three thousand followers, and exterminated every partisan.

sentences.zh: 瀧州蠻陳行範自稱天子，其下何遊魯號定國大將軍，馮璘南越王，破州縣四十。

translations.literal: The Longzhou tribesman Chen Xingfan styled himself Son of Heaven; his subordinates He Youlu called himself Pacification-of-the-State Grand General and Feng Lin King of Nanyue, and they overran forty prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Longzhou tribesman Chen Xingfan declared himself emperor. His lieutenants He Youlu styled himself Pacification-of-the-State Grand General and Feng Lin King of Nanyue, and together they ravaged forty prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 詔思勖發永、道、連三州兵，淮南弩士十萬，襲斬遊魯、璘於陣。

translations.literal: Sixu was ordered to mobilize troops from Yong, Dao, and Lian prefectures and one hundred thousand crossbowmen from Huainan, and in battle he struck down and beheaded Youlu and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Sixu was ordered to raise troops from Yong, Dao, and Lian and one hundred thousand Huainan crossbowmen, and in battle he killed Youlu and Lin.

sentences.zh: 行範走盤遼諸洞，思勖悉眾窮追，生縛之，坑其黨六萬，獲馬金銀鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Xingfan fled to the caves of Panliao and the rest; Sixu pursued with all his forces to the end, captured him alive, buried sixty thousand of his followers alive, and seized horses, gold, and silver in vast amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfan fled into the Panliao caves. Sixu pursued with his full force, took him alive, buried sixty thousand of his followers alive, and seized horses, gold, and silver beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over eighty.

sentences.zh: 思勖鷙忍，敢殺戮，所得俘，必剝面、腦、褫發皮以示人，將士憚服，莫敢視，以是能立功。

translations.literal: Sixu was fierce and cruel, daring in slaughter; captives he took were always flayed of face, brain, and scalp to be displayed. Officers and soldiers feared and submitted, none daring to look—thus he could achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sixu was savage and cruel, relentless in killing. Captives were flayed of face, brain, and scalp for display. His troops feared him and dared not even look—by such means he won his victories.

sentences.zh: 內給事牛仙童納張守珪賂，詔付思勖殺之。

translations.literal: The inner provisioner Niu Xiantong accepted a bribe from Zhang Shougui; an edict handed him to Sixu for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Inner provisioner Niu Xiantong took a bribe from Zhang Shougui; the court ordered Sixu to execute him.

sentences.zh: 思勖縛於格，箠慘不可勝，乃探心，截手足，剔肉以食，肉盡乃得死。

translations.literal: Sixu bound him to a rack and beat him with torments beyond bearing; then he tore out his heart, severed his limbs, stripped the flesh to feed him, and only when the flesh was gone did he die.
translations.idiomatic: Sixu bound him to a rack and beat him past endurance, then tore out his heart, severed his limbs, and carved away the flesh to feed him piece by piece. Only when the flesh was gone did he die.

sentences.zh: 楚客者，樂安人，後歷桂州都督致仕，封松滋縣侯。

translations.literal: Chuke was a man of Le'an; he later served as Guilin regional commander, retired, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke came from Le'an. He later served as Guilin regional commander, retired, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 高力士，馮盎曾孫也。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi was a great-grandson of Feng Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi was a great-grandson of Feng Ang.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，嶺南討擊使李千里上二閹兒，曰金剛，曰力士，武後以其強悟，敕給事左右。

translations.literal: Early in Shengli, the Lingnan punitive commissioner Li Qianli presented two castrated youths named Jingang and Lishi. Empress Wu, finding them strong and quick-witted, ordered them to attend at her side.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shengli the Lingnan punitive commissioner Li Qianli presented two castrated youths, Jingang and Lishi. Empress Wu, impressed by their strength and quick wit, ordered them to attend her.

sentences.zh: 坐累逐出之，中人高延福養為子，故冒其姓。

translations.literal: Through implication in a case he was expelled; the eunuch Gao Yanfu adopted him as a son, and so he took that surname.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in a case, he was expelled. The eunuch Gao Yanfu adopted him as a son, and he took the Gao surname.

sentences.zh: 善武三思，歲餘，復得入禁中，稟食司宮臺。

translations.literal: He won the favor of Wu Sansi; after more than a year he re-entered the inner palace and served in the Palace Provisions Office of the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He won Wu Sansi's favor. After a year he returned to the inner palace and served in the Palace Provisions Office.

sentences.zh: 既壯，長六尺五寸，謹密，善傳詔令，為宮闈丞。

translations.literal: When fully grown he stood six feet five inches, was careful and discreet, skilled at transmitting edicts, and became deputy director of the inner gates.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he stood six feet five, careful and discreet, skilled at relaying edicts, and was made deputy director of the inner gates.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在藩，力士傾心附結，已平韋氏，乃啟屬內坊，擢內給事。

translations.literal: While Xuanzong was still a prince, Lishi devoted himself and attached to him; after the Wei clan was suppressed he petitioned to place him in the inner workshops and promoted him to inner provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was still heir, Lishi gave him his full loyalty. After the Wei clan was overthrown he had him assigned to the inner workshops and promoted him to inner provisioner.

sentences.zh: 先天中，以誅蕭、岑等功為右監門衛將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era, for the merit of executing Xiao and Cen and the rest, he was made Right Gate Guard general and given charge of the Palace Attendants Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian, for helping execute Xiao and Cen and their faction, he was made Right Gate Guard general and put in charge of the Palace Attendants Office.

sentences.zh: 於是四方奏請皆先省後進，小事即專決，雖洗沐未嘗出，眠息殿帷中，僥幸者願一見如天人然。

translations.literal: Thereafter memorials from all quarters were first reviewed by him and then forwarded; minor matters he decided on his own. Even when bathing he never left the palace; he slept within the hall curtains. Those who sought favor longed for a single glimpse as if of a celestial being.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from every quarter passed through him before reaching the throne; minor matters he decided alone. He never left the palace even to bathe and slept within the hall curtains. Favor-seekers yearned for a single glimpse as for a celestial being.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「力士當上，我寢乃安。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When Lishi is on duty above, only then can I sleep at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "With Lishi on watch above, I can sleep in peace."

sentences.zh: 當是時，宇文融、李林甫、蓋嘉運、韋堅、楊慎矜、王鉷、楊國忠、安祿山、安思順、高仙芝等雖以才寵進，然皆厚結力士，故能踵至將相，自餘承風附會不可計，皆得所欲。

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Rong, Li Linfu, Gai Jiayun, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, Yang Guozhong, An Lushan, An Sishun, Gao Xianzhi, and others advanced through talent and favor, yet all cultivated close ties with Lishi and thus in succession reached the ranks of chief minister and general. Countless others who followed the trend and attached themselves likewise obtained what they desired.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong, Li Linfu, Gai Jiayun, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, Yang Guozhong, An Lushan, An Sishun, Gao Xianzhi, and others rose on talent and favor, yet all courted Lishi closely and in turn reached the highest offices. Countless imitators who followed their lead likewise got what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 中人若黎敬仁、林昭隱、尹鳳翔、韓莊、牛仙童、劉奉廷、王承恩、張道斌、李大宜、朱光輝、郭全、邊令誠等，並內供奉，或外監節度軍，脩功德，市鳥獸，皆為之使。

translations.literal: Eunuchs such as Li Jingren, Lin Zhaoyin, Yin Fengxiang, Han Zhuang, Niu Xiantong, Liu Fengting, Wang Chengen, Zhang Daobin, Li Dayi, Zhu Guanghui, Guo Quan, and Bian Lingcheng all served as inner attendants, or supervised military commissioners abroad, built merit works, or purchased birds and beasts—all acted as his agents.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs such as Li Jingren, Lin Zhaoyin, Yin Fengxiang, Han Zhuang, Niu Xiantong, Liu Fengting, Wang Chengen, Zhang Daobin, Li Dayi, Zhu Guanghui, Guo Quan, and Bian Lingcheng served in the inner palace, supervised armies abroad, funded merit works, or bought birds and beasts—all as his agents.

sentences.zh: 使還，所裒獲，動巨萬計，京師甲第池園、良田美產，占者什六，寵與力士略等，然悉藉力士左右輕重乃能然。

translations.literal: When they returned from missions, what they amassed commonly reached tens of thousands; mansions, gardens, fine fields, and prized estates in the capital—six-tenths were held by them. Their favor nearly matched Lishi's, yet all relied on Lishi's influence to tip the scales before they could do so.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, their hauls commonly ran to vast sums. They held six-tenths of the capital's finest mansions, gardens, fields, and estates. Their favor nearly equaled Lishi's, yet all depended on his leverage to make it so.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在東宮，兄事力士，它王、公主呼為翁，戚裏諸家尊曰爹，帝或不名而呼將軍。

translations.literal: When Suzong was crown prince he treated Lishi as an elder brother; other princes and princesses called him Sir; affinal kin addressed him as Father; the emperor sometimes called him General without naming him.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince, Suzong treated Lishi as an elder brother. Other princes and princesses called him Sir, affinal kin called him Father, and the emperor sometimes addressed him simply as General.

sentences.zh: 力士幼與母麥相失，後嶺南節度使得之瀧州，迎還，不復記識，母曰：「胸有七黑子在否？」

translations.literal: In childhood Lishi was separated from his mother Mai; later the Lingnan military commissioner found her in Longzhou and brought her back. He no longer recognized her. His mother said, "Are the seven black moles still on your chest?
translations.idiomatic: As a child Lishi was separated from his mother Mai. Later the Lingnan military commissioner found her in Longzhou and brought her back, but he no longer recognized her. His mother asked, "Are the seven black moles still on your chest?"

sentences.zh: 力士袒示之，如言。

translations.literal: Lishi bared his chest and showed them, just as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi bared his chest and showed them, exactly as she said.

sentences.zh: 母出金環，曰「兒所服者」，乃相持號慟。

translations.literal: His mother produced a gold ring and said, "This is what my son wore," and they embraced and wailed together.
translations.idiomatic: His mother produced a gold ring and said, "This is what my son wore," and they clung to each other, wailing.

sentences.zh: 帝為封越國夫人，而追贈其父廣州大都督。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed her as Lady of Yue and posthumously honored her father as Grand Protector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed her as Lady of Yue and posthumously honored her father as Grand Protector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 延福與妻，及力士貴時故在，侍養與麥均。

translations.literal: Yanfu and his wife, who had been with Lishi when he rose to wealth, were still alive and were cared for on equal terms with Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu and his wife, who had raised Lishi before his rise, were still alive and received the same care as Mai.

sentences.zh: 金吾大將軍程伯獻約力士為兄弟，後麥亡，伯獻缞绖受吊。

translations.literal: The Golden Guard general Cheng Boxian swore brotherhood with Lishi; when Mai later died, Boxian wore mourning hemp and received condolences on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard general Cheng Boxian swore brotherhood with Lishi. When Mai died, Boxian wore mourning and received condolences on Lishi's behalf.

sentences.zh: 河間男子呂玄晤吏京師，女國姝，力士娶之，玄晤擢刀筆史至少卿，子弟仕皆王傅。

translations.literal: A man of Hejian named Lü Xuanwu served as a clerk in the capital; his daughter was a peerless beauty, and Lishi married her. Xuanwu was promoted from clerk to vice minister, and his sons in office all became tutors to princes.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xuanwu of Hejian served as a clerk in the capital. His daughter was renowned for her beauty, and Lishi married her. Xuanwu rose from clerk to vice minister, and his sons in office all became tutors to princes.

sentences.zh: 玄晤妻死，中外贈賻送葬，自第至墓，車徒背相望不絕。

translations.literal: When Xuanwu's wife died, court and commoners sent funeral gifts; from mansion to tomb, carriages and followers stretched back to back without a break.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanwu's wife died, court and commoners sent funeral gifts. From mansion to tomb, carriages and followers stretched unbroken.

sentences.zh: 始，李林甫、牛仙客知帝憚幸東都，而京師漕不給，乃以賦粟助漕，及用和糴法，數年，國用稍充。

translations.literal: At first Li Linfu and Niu Xianke knew the emperor feared traveling to the eastern capital while grain transport to Chang'an fell short; they therefore used tax grain to aid transport and adopted the harmonized-purchase method. After several years state revenues were somewhat replenished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu and Niu Xianke knew the emperor feared traveling east while Chang'an's grain supply lagged. They used tax grain to aid transport and adopted harmonized purchase. After several years the treasury was somewhat replenished.

sentences.zh: 帝齋大同殿，力士侍，帝曰：「我不出長安且十年，海內無事，朕將吐納導引，以天下事付林甫，若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor fasted in the Datong Hall with Lishi in attendance and said, "I have not left Chang'an for nearly ten years; within the seas all is calm. I intend to practice breath regulation and guided exercise and entrust the realm to Linfu—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was fasting in the Datong Hall with Lishi attending and said, "I have scarcely left Chang'an in ten years and the realm is at peace. I mean to devote myself to breath work and guided exercise and leave the empire to Linfu. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 力士對曰：「天子順動，古制也。

translations.literal: Lishi replied, "The Son of Heaven moves with the seasons—this is ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi replied, "The Son of Heaven moves with the seasons—that is ancient law.

sentences.zh: 稅入有常，則人不告勞。

translations.literal: When tax receipts are fixed, the people do not complain of toil.
translations.idiomatic: When tax receipts are fixed, the people do not cry out under the burden.

sentences.zh: 今賦粟充漕，臣恐國無旬月蓄；

translations.literal: Now using tax grain to fill transport quotas—I fear the state will have no store for even a month;
translations.idiomatic: Now tax grain fills transport quotas—I fear the state will have no reserve for even a month;

sentences.zh: 和糴不止，則私藏竭，逐末者眾。

translations.literal: if harmonized purchase does not cease, private stores will be exhausted and those chasing profit will multiply.
translations.idiomatic: if harmonized purchase does not cease, private stores will be drained and profiteers will multiply.

sentences.zh: 又天下柄不可假人，威權既振，孰敢議者！」

translations.literal: Moreover the handle of the realm must not be lent to another; once authority and power are aroused, who will dare speak against it!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the reins of empire must not be lent away. Once authority is aroused, who will dare object!"

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，力士頓首自陳「心狂易，語謬當死」。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased. Lishi kowtowed and confessed himself: "My mind is rash and erratic; my words were wrong and I deserve death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased. Lishi kowtowed and said, "My mind is rash; my words were wrong and I deserve death."

sentences.zh: 帝為置酒，左右呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor had wine set out, and those at his side cried "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had wine brought, and attendants cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 由是還內宅，不復事。

translations.literal: From this he returned to his inner residence and no longer attended to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he withdrew to his private residence and no longer handled affairs.

sentences.zh: 加累驃騎大將軍，封渤海郡公。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Cavalry-in-Chief General and enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Cavalry-in-Chief General and enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 於來廷坊建佛祠，興寧坊立道士祠，珍樓寶屋，國貲所不逮。

translations.literal: In Laiting Ward he built a Buddhist shrine; in Xingning Ward he erected a Daoist temple—treasured towers and jeweled halls beyond what the state treasury could match.
translations.idiomatic: In Laiting Ward he built a Buddhist shrine; in Xingning Ward a Daoist temple—treasured towers and jeweled halls the state treasury could not rival.

sentences.zh: 鍾成，力士宴公卿，一扣鍾，納禮錢十萬，有佞悅者至二十扣，其少亦不減十。

translations.literal: When the bell was completed, Lishi feasted chief ministers and nobles; one strike of the bell required a gift of one hundred thousand cash. Flatterers gave up to twenty strikes; even the least gave no fewer than ten.
translations.idiomatic: When the bell was finished, Lishi feasted the chief ministers. One strike cost one hundred thousand cash in gifts. Flatterers struck it twenty times; even the stingiest gave ten.

sentences.zh: 都北堰澧列五硙，日僦三百斛直。

translations.literal: North of the capital he dammed the Li and set up five millstones, renting them daily for the price of three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: North of the capital he dammed the Li and set up five millstones, renting them daily for three hundred bushels' worth.

sentences.zh: 有袁思藝者，帝亦愛幸，然驕倨甚，士大夫疏畏之，而力士陰巧得人譽。

translations.literal: There was a Yuan Siyi whom the emperor also loved and favored, but he was extremely arrogant; scholar-officials kept their distance and feared him, while Lishi was quietly skillful and gained people's praise.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Yuan Siyi whom the emperor also loved and favored, but he was extremely arrogant; scholar-officials kept their distance and feared him, while Lishi was quietly skillful and gained people's praise.

sentences.zh: 帝初置內侍省監二員，秩三品，以力士、思藝為之。

translations.literal: When the emperor first established two supervisors in the Palace Domestic Service, with rank of the third grade, he appointed Lishi and Siyi to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first established two supervisors in the Palace Domestic Service, with rank of the third grade, he appointed Lishi and Siyi to the posts.

sentences.zh: 帝幸蜀，思藝遂臣賊，而力士從帝，進齊國公。

translations.literal: When the emperor fled to Shu, Siyi submitted to the rebels, but Lishi followed the emperor and was advanced to Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Shu, Siyi submitted to the rebels, but Lishi followed the emperor and was advanced to Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝聞肅宗即位，喜曰：「吾兒應天順人，改元至德，不忘孝乎，尚何憂？」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Suzong had taken the throne, he rejoiced and said, "My son has answered Heaven and followed the people, changing the era name to Zhide; has he not remembered filial duty? What is there still to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Suzong had taken the throne, he rejoiced and said, "My son has answered Heaven and followed the people, changing the era name to Zhide; has he not remembered filial duty? What is there still to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 力士曰：「兩京失守，生人流亡，河南漢北為戰區，天下痛心，而陛下以為何憂，臣不敢聞。」

translations.literal: Lishi said, "The two capitals have fallen, the living people have scattered as refugees, Henan and the north of the Han are battle zones, and all under Heaven grieves. Yet Your Majesty says, 'What is there to worry about?' Your subject dares not hear it."
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "The two capitals have fallen, the living people have scattered as refugees, Henan and the north of the Han are battle zones, and all under Heaven grieves. Yet Your Majesty says, 'What is there to worry about?' Your subject dares not hear it."

sentences.zh: 從上皇還，進開府儀同三司，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: After returning with the Retired Emperor, he was advanced to Kaifu Yitong Sansi and given an actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After returning with the Retired Emperor, he was advanced to Kaifu Yitong Sansi and given an actual fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 上皇徙西內，居十日，為李輔國所誣，除籍，長流巫州。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor was moved to the Western Palace and had been there ten days, Lishi was falsely accused by Li Fuguo, struck from the registers, and permanently exiled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor was moved to the Western Palace and had been there ten days, Lishi was falsely accused by Li Fuguo, struck from the registers, and permanently exiled to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 力士方逃瘧功巨閣下，輔國以詔召，力士趨至閣外，遣內養授謫制，因曰：「巨當死已久，天子哀憐至今日，願一見陛下顏色，死不恨。」

translations.literal: Lishi was then avoiding malaria below Gongju Pavilion when Fuguo summoned him by edict. Lishi hurried outside the pavilion, and an inner attendant was sent to deliver the demotion order. Lishi then said, "I deserved death long ago, yet the Son of Heaven has pitied me until today. I wish only to see His Majesty's face once; then I would die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Lishi was then avoiding malaria below Gongju Pavilion when Fuguo summoned him by edict. Lishi hurried outside the pavilion, and an inner attendant was sent to deliver the demotion order. Lishi then said, "I deserved death long ago, yet the Son of Heaven has pitied me until today. I wish only to see His Majesty's face once; then I would die without regret."

sentences.zh: 輔國不許。

translations.literal: Fuguo did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年赦還，見二帝遺詔，北向哭歐血，曰：「大行升遐，不得攀梓宮，死有餘恨。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he returned under amnesty. When he saw the final edicts of the two emperors, he faced north, wept until he spat blood, and said, "The departed sovereigns have ascended far away, and I could not cling to their coffins. In death I will still have lasting regret."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying he returned under amnesty. When he saw the final edicts of the two emperors, he faced north, wept until he spat blood, and said, "The departed sovereigns have ascended far away, and I could not cling to their coffins. In death I will still have lasting regret."

sentences.zh: 慟而卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died in grief at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in grief at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 代宗以護衛先帝勞，還其官，贈揚州大都督，陪葬泰陵。

translations.literal: Because of his service in guarding the former emperor, Daizong restored his offices, posthumously granted him the title Grand Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and had him buried beside Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his service in guarding the former emperor, Daizong restored his offices, posthumously granted him the title Grand Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and had him buried beside Tailing.

sentences.zh: 初，太子瑛廢，武惠妃方嬖，李林甫等皆屬壽王，帝以肅宗長，意未決，居忽忽不食。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Crown Prince Ying was deposed, Consort Wu Hui was in favor and Li Linfu and others all backed Prince Shou; the emperor, seeing that Suzong was eldest, had not yet decided, and sat listless, refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Ying was deposed, Consort Wu Hui was in favor and Li Linfu backed Prince Shou. The emperor, noting that Suzong was eldest, had not decided and sat listless, refusing food.

sentences.zh: 力士曰：「大家不食，亦膳羞不具耶？」

translations.literal: Lishi said, "Your Majesty does not eat—is it that the dishes are not prepared?
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "Your Majesty will not eat—is the fare not prepared?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾，我家老，揣我何為而然？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You are an elder of our household—can you not guess why I am like this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are an elder of our house—cannot you guess why I am like this?"

sentences.zh: 力士曰：「嗣君未定耶？

translations.literal: Lishi said, "Has the heir not yet been settled?
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "Has the heir not been settled?

sentences.zh: 推長而立，孰敢爭？」

translations.literal: Establish the eldest—who would dare contend?"
translations.idiomatic: Install the eldest son—who would dare contest it?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 儲位遂定。

translations.literal: Thus the succession was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the succession was settled.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，邊將爭立功，帝嘗曰：「朕春秋高，朝廷細務付宰相，蕃夷不龔付諸將，寧不暇耶？」

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era frontier generals vied for merit. The emperor once said, "I am advanced in years; court details I leave to the chief minister, and the barbarians beyond I entrust to the generals—would I not have leisure?
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao frontier generals vied for glory. The emperor once said, "I am old; court details go to the chief minister and the frontier to the generals—should I not have leisure?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣間至閣門，見奏事者言雲南數喪師，又北兵悍且強，陛下何以制之？

translations.literal: He replied, "When I pass by the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat I hear memorialists say Yunnan has repeatedly lost armies, and the northern troops are fierce and strong—how will Your Majesty control them?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Passing the Secretariat gate I hear memorialists say Yunnan has lost armies again and again, and the northern troops are fierce and strong—how will Your Majesty control them?

sentences.zh: 臣恐禍成不可禁。」

translations.literal: I fear disaster will form and cannot be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: I fear disaster will take shape beyond restraint."

sentences.zh: 其指蓋謂祿山。

translations.literal: His meaning was presumably Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Lushan.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿勿言，朕將圖之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Say no more; I shall plan for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Say no more. I shall deal with it."

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，大雨，帝顧左右無人，即曰：「天方災，卿宜言之。」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, during heavy rains, the emperor looked about and, seeing no one else near, said at once, "Heaven is sending disaster—you should speak."
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, during heavy rains, the emperor glanced about, saw no one else near, and said, "Heaven is sending disaster—you should speak."

sentences.zh: 力士曰：「自陛下以權假宰相，法令不行，陰陽失度，天下事庸可復安？

translations.literal: Lishi said, "Since Your Majesty lent authority to the chief minister, laws and edicts are not enforced, yin and yang have lost their measure—how can affairs under Heaven ever be at peace again?
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "Since Your Majesty lent power to the chief minister, laws go unenforced and yin and yang are out of balance—how can the realm ever be at peace again?

sentences.zh: 臣之鉗口，其時也。」

translations.literal: That I held my tongue—its time had come."
translations.idiomatic: That I held my tongue—its time had come."

sentences.zh: 帝不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 明年祿山反。

translations.literal: The next year Lushan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Lushan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 力士善揣時事勢候相上下，雖親昵，至當覆敗，不肯為救力，故生平無顯顯大過。

translations.literal: Lishi was skilled at gauging the times and reading the rise and fall of fortunes; even with those he was intimate, when ruin was due he would not exert himself to save them. Thus in his lifetime he had no glaring great faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi was skilled at reading the times and fortunes of men. Even with intimates, when ruin was due he would not lift a hand to save them. Thus he committed no glaring great fault in his life.

sentences.zh: 議者頗恨宇文融以來權利相賊，階天下之禍，雖有補益，弗相除雲。

translations.literal: Critics greatly resented that from Yuwen Rong onward power and profit devoured one another and escalated the realm's disaster; though there were some benefits, they did not offset the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Critics resented that from Yuwen Rong onward men devoured one another for power and profit, escalating the empire's ruin. Any good they did not cancel the harm.

sentences.zh: 程元振，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanzhen was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少以宦人直內侍省，遷內射生使、飛龍廄副使。

translations.literal: In youth as a eunuch he was stationed at the Directorate of Palace Attendants; he was transferred to Internal Archery Corps commander and deputy commissioner of the Flying Dragon Stable.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as a eunuch in the Directorate of Palace Attendants, then rose to commander of the Internal Archery Corps and deputy commissioner of the Flying Dragon Stable.

sentences.zh: 張皇后謀立越王，元振見太子，發其奸，與李輔國助討難，立太子，是為代宗。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhang plotted to install the Prince of Yue, Yuanzhen saw the Crown Prince, exposed her treachery, and with Li Fuguo aided in suppressing the crisis and installing the Crown Prince, who became Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zhang plotted to put the Prince of Yue on the throne, Yuanzhen went to the Crown Prince, exposed the conspiracy, and together with Li Fuguo helped put down the crisis and elevate the Crown Prince, who became Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 拜右監門衛將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Gates Guards and made acting head of the Palace Attendants Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Right Gates Guards and placed in charge of the Palace Attendants Directorate.

sentences.zh: 帝以藥子昂判元帥行軍司馬，固辭，乃以命元振，封保定縣侯。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to assign Yao Zi'ang as chief administrator of the marshal's campaign staff; he firmly declined, and the appointment was then given to Yuanzhen, who was enfeoffed as Marquis of Baoding County.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to appoint Yao Zi'ang chief administrator of the marshal's campaign staff, but Yao firmly declined; the post was then given to Yuanzhen, who was enfeoffed as Marquis of Baoding County.

sentences.zh: 再遷驃騎大將軍、邠國公，盡總禁兵。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Bin, and came to command all the palace guard entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Bin, assuming full command of the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 不逾歲，權震天下，在輔國右，兇決又過之，軍中呼十郎。

translations.literal: Within less than a year, his power shook the realm; he stood above Fuguo, and in vicious decisiveness he surpassed him still; in the army he was called Tenth Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year his authority overshadowed the empire. He outranked Fuguo and was even more ruthless; the troops called him "Young Master Ten."

sentences.zh: 王仲升者，初為淮西節度使，與襄州張維瑾部將戰申州，被執。

translations.literal: There was Wang Zhongsheng, who had first served as military governor of Huai West; he fought at Shen Province with a subordinate general of Zhang Weijin of Xiang Prefecture and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsheng had first served as military governor of Huai West. In battle at Shen Province against a subordinate general of Zhang Weijin of Xiangzhou, he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 賊平，元振薦為右羽林大將軍兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Yuanzhen recommended him as General-in-Chief of the Right Forest Guards concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was put down, Yuanzhen recommended him for the posts of General-in-Chief of the Right Forest Guards and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 將軍兼大夫由仲升始。

translations.literal: General concurrently Grand Censor began with Zhongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The combination of general and censor-in-chief began with Zhongsheng.

sentences.zh: 裴冕與元振忤，乃掎韓穎等罪貶施州。

translations.literal: Pei Mian crossed Yuanzhen; he then seized on the crimes of Han Ying and others and had them demoted to Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Mian fell out with Yuanzhen, Yuanzhen seized on charges against Han Ying and others and had them banished to Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 來瑱守襄、漢有功，元振嘗諉屬，不應，因仲升共誣殺瑱。

translations.literal: Lai Tian had merit in defending Xiang and Han; Yuanzhen had once entrusted tasks to him but received no response, and together with Zhongsheng falsely accused and killed Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian had distinguished himself defending Xiang and Han. Yuanzhen had tried to recruit him without success; he then joined with Zhongsheng to frame and execute Tian.

sentences.zh: 同華節度使李懷讓被構，憂甚自殺。

translations.literal: Li Huairang, military governor of Tong and Hua, was framed; in deep distress he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huairang, military governor of Tonghua, was framed and, in anguish, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 素惡李光弼，數媒蠍以疑之。

translations.literal: He had long hated Li Guangbi, and repeatedly spread poison through rumors to arouse suspicion against him.
translations.idiomatic: He had long hated Li Guangbi and repeatedly planted poisonous rumors to turn the court against him.

sentences.zh: 瑱等上將，冕、光弼元勛，既誅斥，或不自省，方帥繇是攜解。

translations.literal: Tian and others were top generals; Mian and Guangbi were founding meritorious men—once executed and expelled, Yuanzhen perhaps did not examine himself; from this the regional commanders drew apart in discord.
translations.idiomatic: After top generals like Tian were killed and founding heroes like Pei Mian and Li Guangbi driven out, Yuanzhen showed no self-reflection, and regional commanders drifted apart in mutual distrust.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃、党項內侵，詔集天下兵，無一士奔命者。

translations.literal: In the early Guangde era, Tibetans and Tangut tribes invaded inward; an edict summoned troops from throughout the realm, yet not a single soldier came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde reign the Tibetans and Tanguts invaded. An imperial summons went out for troops from across the empire, but not a single man answered the call.

sentences.zh: 虜扣便橋，帝倉黃出居陜，京師陷，賊剽府庫，焚閭弄，蕭然為空。

translations.literal: The foe pressed upon Bian Bridge; the emperor fled in panic to settle at Shan; the capital fell; the bandits looted the treasury stores and burned lanes and alleys until all was desolate and empty.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy reached Bian Bridge. The emperor fled in panic to Shanzhou; Chang'an fell. Raiders emptied the treasuries and burned streets and lanes until the city lay desolate.

sentences.zh: 於是太常博士、翰林待詔柳伉上疏曰：「犬戎以數萬眾犯關度隴，歷秦、渭，掠邠、涇，不血刃而入京師，謀臣不奮一言，武士不力一戰，提卒叫呼，劫宮闈，焚陵寢，此將帥叛陛下也；

translations.literal: Then the Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Hanlin draft edict-writer Liu Kuang submitted a memorial saying: "The dog Rong with tens of thousands violated the passes and crossed Long, passed through Qin and Wei, plundered Bin and Jing, and entered the capital without drawing blood; strategists did not rouse a single word, warriors did not exert a single battle—troops they led raised clamor, seized the palace precincts, and burned the imperial tombs: this is the generals betraying Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Kuang, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Hanlin draft edict writer, submitted a memorial: "Tens of thousands of barbarians crossed the passes and the Long Mountains, swept through Qin and Wei, ravaged Bin and Jing, and took Chang'an without a fight. No strategist spoke up; no warrior fought. Led troops raised a clamor, seized the palace, and burned the imperial tombs—your generals have betrayed you;

sentences.zh: 自朝義之滅，陛下以為智力所能，故疏元功，委近習，日引月長以成大禍，群臣在廷無一犯顏回慮者，此公卿叛陛下也；

translations.literal: Since Chaoyi's destruction, Your Majesty believed it within your own wisdom and power, and so distanced founding meritorious men, entrusted affairs to close attendants, and day by day and month by month let great calamity grow; among the ministers at court not one dared to offend your countenance and turn back to consider—this is the high officials betraying Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: Since Chaoyi's defeat you have believed your own wit and power sufficient, distanced founding heroes, and entrusted affairs to close attendants until disaster grew day by day. Not one minister in court dared speak plainly—your high officials have betrayed you;

sentences.zh: 陛下始出都，百姓填然奪府庫，相殺戮，此三輔叛陛下也；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first left the capital, the common people surged to seize the treasury stores and slaughter one another—this is the Three Metropolises betraying Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: When you first fled the capital, the people surged to loot the treasuries and kill one another—the capital region has betrayed you;

sentences.zh: 自十月朔召諸道兵，盡四十日，無只輪入關者，此四方叛陛下也。

translations.literal: From the first day of the tenth month troops were summoned from all circuits; through forty full days not a single wheel entered the passes—this is the four quarters betraying Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Since the first of the tenth month you have summoned troops from every circuit; for forty days not a single wheel has crossed the passes—the whole empire has betrayed you.

sentences.zh: 內外離叛，雖一魚朝恩以陜郡戮力，陛下獨能以此守社稷乎？

translations.literal: Within and without there is separation and rebellion; though Yu Chao'en alone exerts himself with Shan Prefecture, can Your Majesty alone with this preserve the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: Inside and out the realm has turned against you. Though Yu Chao'en alone holds Shan Prefecture with all his strength, can you alone preserve the dynasty on that?

sentences.zh: 陛下以今日勢為安耶？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty regard the present situation as secure?
translations.idiomatic: Do you consider the present situation secure?

sentences.zh: 危耶？

translations.literal: Or perilous?
translations.idiomatic: Or perilous?

sentences.zh: 若以為危，豈得高枕不為天下計？

translations.literal: If you regard it as perilous, how can you rest at ease on a high pillow and not plan for the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If you see peril, how can you rest easy and make no plans for the realm?

sentences.zh: 臣聞良醫療疾，當病飲藥，藥不當疾，猶無益也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that a good physician treats illness: when there is disease one takes medicine; if the medicine does not match the disease, it is still of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a good physician treats disease by prescribing medicine suited to the illness; the wrong medicine does no good at all.

sentences.zh: 陛下視今日病何繇至此乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, consider: by what path did today's disease reach this point?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, how did the disease reach this point?

sentences.zh: 天下之心，乃恨陛下遠賢良，任宦豎，離間將相而幾於亡。

translations.literal: The heart of the realm hates that Your Majesty keeps the worthy and good at a distance, employs eunuch attendants, and sets generals and chancellors against one another until the state nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: The people blame you for keeping the worthy at arm's length, trusting eunuch attendants, and driving generals and chancellors apart until the dynasty nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 必欲存宗廟社稷，獨斬元振首，馳告天下，悉出內使隸諸州，獨留朝恩備左右，陛下持神策兵付大臣，然後削尊號，下詔引咎，率德勵行，屏嬪妃，任將相。

translations.literal: If you must preserve the ancestral temples and altars of state, cut off Yuanzhen's head alone, dispatch riders to announce it throughout the realm, send out all inner attendants to be placed under the various prefectures, keep Chao'en alone to attend at your side, hand the Divine Strategy Army to great ministers—then reduce your honorific titles, issue an edict accepting blame, lead in virtue and encourage right conduct, dismiss consorts and concubines, and employ generals and chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish to save the dynasty, execute Yuanzhen alone and proclaim it to the realm. Send all inner attendants out to the prefectures, keep only Chao'en at your side, and place the Divine Strategy Army in the hands of your ministers. Then reduce your honorific titles, issue an edict accepting blame, lead by virtue, dismiss your consorts, and trust generals and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 若曰『天下其許朕自新改過乎，宜即募士西與朝廷會；

translations.literal: If you say, 'Will the realm allow Us to renew Ourselves and reform Our faults? Then let men be recruited at once to march west and join the court;
translations.idiomatic: Say: 'Will the realm allow me to reform? Then let men be recruited at once to march west and join the court;

sentences.zh: 若以朕惡未悛耶，則帝王大器，敢妨聖賢，其聽天下所往。』

translations.literal: If you say, 'If Our faults are not yet reformed, then the great vessel of kingship—dare it obstruct the sage and worthy? Let the realm go where it will.'
translations.idiomatic: if my faults are beyond reform, then the throne must not stand in the way of worthier men—let the realm choose its own course.'

sentences.zh: 如此而兵不至，人不感，天下不服，請赤臣族以謝。」

translations.literal: If after this troops still do not come, the people are not moved, and the realm does not submit, your subject asks that his clan be wiped out to atone.
translations.idiomatic: If after that troops still do not come, the people are unmoved, and the realm will not submit, I ask that my entire clan be executed in atonement."

sentences.zh: 疏聞，帝顧公議不與，乃下詔盡削元振官爵，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, the emperor looked to public opinion and did not agree; he then issued an edict stripping Yuanzhen of all offices and titles and sending him back to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the emperor looked to public opinion and did not agree; he issued an edict stripping Yuanzhen of all offices and titles and sending him back to his estate.

sentences.zh: 帝還，元振自三原衣婦衣私入京師，舍司農卿陳景詮家，圖不軌。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, Yuanzhen from Sanyuan put on women's clothing and secretly entered the capital, lodged at the home of Minister of Revenue Chen Jingquan, and plotted sedition.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Yuanzhen left Sanyuan disguised in women's clothing, slipped into the capital, and lodged with Minister of Revenue Chen Jingquan to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 御史劾按，長流溱州，景詮貶新興尉。

translations.literal: Censors investigated and impeached him; he was exiled far to Qin Prefecture, and Jingquan was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Censors investigated the case. Yuanzhen was exiled to Qin Prefecture, and Jingquan was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 元振行至江陵死。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen died on the road at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen died en route at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時又有駱奉先者，亦三原人，歷右驍衛大將軍，數從帝討伐，尤見幸，廣德初，監仆固懷恩軍者。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Luo Fengxian, likewise a man of Sanyuan, who had served as General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry; he repeatedly followed the emperor on campaigns and was especially favored; in early Guangde he was the one supervising Pugu Huai'en's army.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Luo Fengxian of Sanyuan, who had risen to General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry. He campaigned repeatedly with the emperor and enjoyed special favor. In early Guangde he was assigned to supervise Pugu Huai'en's army.

sentences.zh: 奉先恃恩貪甚，懷恩不平，既而懼其譖，遂叛。

translations.literal: Fengxian relied on favor and was extremely greedy; Huai'en was resentful, and then fearing his slander, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian abused imperial favor and grew rapacious. Huai'en resented him, then fearing slander, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 事平，擢奉先軍容使，掌畿內兵，權焰熾然。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Fengxian was promoted to Army Inspector and put in charge of troops within the capital region; his power blazed fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was put down, Fengxian was promoted to Army Inspector and given command of the capital armies; his power burned bright.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，以吐蕃數驚京師，始城鄠，以奉先為使，悉毀縣外廬舍，無尺椽。

translations.literal: In early Yongtai, because Tibetans repeatedly alarmed the capital, they first fortified E; Fengxian was made commissioner, and all dwellings outside the county were destroyed until not a beam remained.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yongtai, with Tibetans repeatedly threatening the capital, the court fortified E and appointed Fengxian commissioner. Every dwelling outside the county was torn down until not a beam remained.

sentences.zh: 累封江國公，監鳳翔軍，大歷末卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Jiang, supervised the Fengxiang army, and died at the end of the Dali era.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Jiang, supervised the Fengxiang army, and died near the end of the Dali reign.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩，瀘州瀘川人。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en was a native of Luchuan in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en came from Luchuan in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，以品官給事黃門，內陰黠，善宣納詔令。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, as a ranked official he served in the Yellow Gate; inwardly he was secretive and cunning, and skilled at proclaiming and conveying edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he served in the Yellow Gate as a ranked official. Secretive and cunning by nature, he was skilled at proclaiming imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 至德初，監李光進軍。

translations.literal: In early Zhide he supervised Li Guangjin's army.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhide he was assigned to supervise Li Guangjin's army.

sentences.zh: 京師平，為三宮檢責使，以左監門衛將軍知內侍省事。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he became inspector of the Three Palaces and, as General of the Left Gates Guards, acted as head of the Palace Attendants Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was recovered, he became inspector of the Three Palaces and, as General of the Left Gates Guards, took charge of the Palace Attendants Directorate.

sentences.zh: 九節度圍賊相州，以朝恩為觀軍容、宣慰、處置使。

translations.literal: When nine military governors besieged the rebels at Xiang Prefecture, Chao'en was made Army Inspector, Pacification Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When nine military governors besieged the rebels at Xiangzhou, Chao'en was appointed Army Inspector, Pacification Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使自朝恩始。

translations.literal: Army Inspector began with Chao'en.
translations.idiomatic: The post of Army Inspector began with Chao'en.

sentences.zh: 史思明攻洛陽，朝恩以神策兵屯陜。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming attacked Luoyang, Chao'en stationed the Divine Strategy Army at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming attacked Luoyang, Chao'en encamped the Divine Strategy Army at Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 洛陽陷，思明長驅至硤石，使子朝義為遊軍。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, Siming drove straight to Xiashi and sent his son Chaoyi as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, Siming drove straight to Xiashi and sent his son Chaoyi ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔銳兵十萬循渭而東以濟師。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong ordered a hundred thousand elite troops to follow the Wei eastward to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong ordered a hundred thousand elite troops to march east along the Wei to reinforce the army.

sentences.zh: 朝恩按兵陜東，使神策將衛伯玉與賊將康文景等戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Chao'en held his troops east of Shan and sent the Divine Strategy general Wei Boyu to fight the rebel generals Kang Wenjing and others, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en held his army east of Shan and sent Divine Strategy general Wei Boyu against the rebel generals Kang Wenjing and others, defeating them.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平，徙屯汴州，加開府儀同三司，封馮翊郡公。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, he moved his encampment to Bian Prefecture, was given the honorary title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Purse, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang was recovered, he moved his camp to Bianzhou, was granted the honorary title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Purse, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，還屯陜。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era he returned to encamp at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying reign he returned to encamp at Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗避吐蕃東幸，衛兵離散，朝恩悉軍奉迎華陰，乘輿六師乃振，帝德之，更號天下觀軍容、宣慰、處置使，專領神策軍，賞賜不涯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong fled east to escape the Tibetans, the guard troops scattered; Chao'en led his entire army to welcome him at Huayin, and only then did the imperial carriage and the Six Armies recover their strength; the emperor was grateful to him, changed his title to Army Inspector, Pacification Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner for All Under Heaven, put him solely in command of the Divine Strategy Army, and rewarded him without limit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong fled east before the Tibetans, the imperial guard scattered. Chao'en brought his entire army to welcome him at Huayin, restoring order to the imperial procession and the Six Armies. Grateful, the emperor renamed him Army Inspector, Pacification Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner for All Under Heaven, gave him sole command of the Divine Strategy Army, and showered him with rewards.

sentences.zh: 朝恩資小人，恃功岸忽無所憚。

translations.literal: Chao'en by nature was a petty man; relying on his merit, he was haughty and insolent without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en was a petty man by nature. Flush with merit, he grew haughty and insolent, fearing nothing.

sentences.zh: 仆固玚攻絳州，使姚良據溫，誘回紇陷河陽。

translations.literal: Pugu Yang attacked Jiang Prefecture, had Yao Liang hold Wen, and induced the Uyghurs to seize Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Yang attacked Jiangzhou, had Yao Liang hold Wen, and induced the Uyghurs to seize Heyang.

sentences.zh: 朝恩遣李忠誠討玚，以霍文場監之；

translations.literal: Chao'en sent Li Zhongcheng to suppress Yang, with Huo Wenchang supervising him;
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en sent Li Zhongcheng to suppress Yang, with Huo Wenchang supervising;

sentences.zh: 王景岑討良，王希遷監之。

translations.literal: Wang Jingcen was sent to suppress Liang, with Wang Xiqian supervising.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingcen was sent to suppress Liang, with Wang Xiqian supervising.

sentences.zh: 敗玚於萬泉，生擒良。

translations.literal: Yang was defeated at Wanquan, and Liang was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was defeated at Wanquan, and Liang was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 高暉等引吐蕃入寇，遣劉德信討斬之。

translations.literal: Gao Hui and others led Tibetans in invasion; he dispatched Liu Dexin to suppress and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Hui and others led Tibetans in an invasion, he dispatched Liu Dexin to suppress and execute them.

sentences.zh: 故朝恩因麾下數克獲，竊以自高。

translations.literal: Thus Chao'en, because his subordinates repeatedly achieved captures, secretly took pride in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because his subordinates repeatedly won victories, Chao'en secretly grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 是時郭子儀有定天下功，居人臣第一，心冒之，乘相州敗，鬼為詆譖，肅宗不內其語，然猶罷子信兵，留京師。

translations.literal: At this time Guo Ziyi had the merit of settling the realm and stood first among subjects; Chao'en envied him in his heart; taking advantage of the defeat at Xiang Prefecture, he secretly slandered him; Emperor Suzong did not accept his words inwardly, yet still stripped Ziyi of his troops and kept him in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi had by then pacified the realm and stood first among the emperor's subjects. Chao'en envied him and, exploiting the defeat at Xiangzhou, secretly slandered him. Emperor Suzong did not believe the charges, but still stripped Ziyi of his command and kept him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，與程元振一口加毀，帝未及寤，子儀憂甚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended, he and Cheng Yuanzhen together added slander with one voice; the emperor had not yet awakened to it, and Ziyi was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended, Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen joined in slandering Ziyi. The emperor had not yet seen through them, and Ziyi was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 俄而吐蕃陷京師，卒用其力，王室再安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Tibetans seized the capital; in the end his strength was used, and the royal house was again secured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tibetans seized Chang'an, and in the end the court had to rely on his strength to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 故朝恩內慚，乃勸帝徙洛陽，欲遠戎狄。

translations.literal: Thus Chao'en was inwardly ashamed, and so urged the emperor to move the capital to Luoyang, wishing to keep distant from the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed at this, Chao'en urged the emperor to move the capital to Luoyang to put distance between the court and the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 百僚在廷，朝恩從十餘人持兵出，曰：「虜數犯都甸，欲幸洛，雲何？」

translations.literal: With the hundred officials in court, Chao'en came out with more than ten men bearing arms and said, "The barbarians repeatedly violate the capital region; We wish to visit Luoyang—what say you?
translations.idiomatic: With the full court assembled, Chao'en emerged with more than ten armed followers and said, "The barbarians repeatedly threaten the capital. I wish to move the court to Luoyang—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 宰相未對，有近臣折曰：「敕使反耶？

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not reply; a close attendant sharply said, "Has the edict-bearer rebelled?
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers did not answer. A close attendant sharply replied, "Has the imperial envoy rebelled?

sentences.zh: 今屯兵足以捍寇，何遽脅天子棄宗廟為？」

translations.literal: The troops now encamped are sufficient to repel the foe—why suddenly coerce the Son of Heaven to abandon the ancestral temples?
translations.idiomatic: The troops now encamped are enough to repel the enemy—why suddenly coerce the emperor to abandon the ancestral temples?"

sentences.zh: 朝恩色沮，而子儀亦謂不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Chao'en's countenance fell, and Ziyi also said it could not be done, and so the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en's face fell. Ziyi also said it could not be done, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 朝恩好引輕浮後生處門下，講《五經》大義，作文章，謂才兼文武，僥伺誤寵。

translations.literal: Chao'en liked to bring frivolous young men under his patronage, lecture on the great meaning of the Five Classics, compose essays, and claim talent in both civil and military affairs, hoping by chance to win mistaken favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en liked to gather frivolous young men under his patronage, lecture on the Five Classics, compose essays, and claim to combine civil and military talent, hoping by chance to win misplaced favor.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，詔判國子監，兼鴻臚、禮賓、內飛龍、閑廄使，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: In Yongtai he was ordered to administer the Directorate of Education, concurrently serving as commissioner of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, Protocol Reception, Internal Flying Dragon Stable, and Imperial Stud, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongtai he was ordered to administer the Directorate of Education while concurrently serving as commissioner of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, Protocol Reception, Internal Flying Dragon Stable, and Imperial Stud, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 始詣學，詔宰相、常參官、六軍將軍悉集，京兆設食，內教坊出音樂俳倡侑宴，大臣子弟二百人，朱紫雜然為附學生，列廡次。

translations.literal: When he first visited the academy, an edict ordered chief ministers, regular attendees at court, and generals of the Six Armies all to assemble; the capital prefecture provided food; the Inner Music Office sent musicians and performers to entertain the banquet; two hundred sons of great ministers, mixed in red and purple, served as attached students and lined the corridors in order.
translations.idiomatic: On his first visit to the academy, an edict summoned chief ministers, regular court officials, and generals of the Six Armies. The capital prefecture provided a feast; the Inner Music Office sent musicians and performers. Two hundred sons of great ministers, dressed in red and purple, served as attached students and lined the corridors.

sentences.zh: 又賜錢千萬，取子錢供秩飯。

translations.literal: He was also granted ten million in cash; the interest was taken to supply stipends and meals.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted ten million in cash, the interest from which supplied stipends and meals.

sentences.zh: 每視學，從神策兵數百，京兆尹黎幹率錢勞從者，一費數十萬，而朝恩色常不足。

translations.literal: Each time he inspected the academy, several hundred Divine Strategy troops followed him; the capital prefect Li Gan led in cash to reward the followers—one occasion cost several hundred thousand—yet Chao'en's expression was often dissatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he inspected the academy, several hundred Divine Strategy troops accompanied him. Capital Prefect Li Gan led contributions of cash to reward the retinue—one visit cost several hundred thousand—yet Chao'en's expression was often dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 凡詔會群臣計事，朝恩怙貴，誕辭折愧坐人出其上，雖元載辯強亦拱默，唯禮部郎中相裏造、殿中侍御史李衎酬詰往返，未始降屈，朝恩不懌，黜衎以動造。

translations.literal: Whenever an edict summoned the ministers to plan affairs, Chao'en relied on his eminence; with extravagant words he shamed those seated and put them beneath him—even Yuan Zai, strong in debate, bowed in silence; only Bureau Director of Rites Xiangli Zao and Palace Censor Li Kan exchanged rebuttals back and forth and never lowered themselves; Chao'en was displeased and demoted Kan to move against Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court assembled ministers to deliberate, Chao'en relied on his rank and with grandiose speech humiliated those present, putting himself above them. Even Yuan Zai, a formidable debater, bowed in silence. Only Bureau Director of Rites Xiangli Zao and Palace Censor Li Kan answered him back without yielding. Chao'en was displeased and demoted Kan to pressure Zao.

sentences.zh: 又謀將易執政以震朝廷，乃會百官都堂，且言：「宰相者，和元氣，輯群生。

translations.literal: He also plotted to replace the chief ministers to shake the court; he then assembled all officials in the chief hall and said: "The chief minister harmonizes the primordial qi and gathers the multitude of living beings.
translations.idiomatic: He also plotted to replace the chief ministers and shake the court. He assembled all officials in the chief hall and said, "The chief minister harmonizes the primordial qi and gathers the multitude of living beings.

sentences.zh: 今水旱不時，屯軍數十萬，饋運困竭，天子臥不安席，宰相何以輔之？

translations.literal: Now floods and droughts come untimely, encamped armies number several hundred thousand, supply transport is exhausted and depleted, the Son of Heaven lies on his bed unable to rest at ease—how do the chief ministers assist him?
translations.idiomatic: Now floods and droughts come untimely, hundreds of thousands of troops are encamped, supply lines are exhausted, and the emperor cannot rest at ease—how are the chief ministers assisting him?

sentences.zh: 不退避賢路，默默尚何賴乎？」

translations.literal: If they do not withdraw and yield the path of the worthy, in silence what is there still to rely on?
translations.idiomatic: If they will not step aside for the worthy, what use is their silent presence?"

sentences.zh: 宰相俯首，坐皆失色。

translations.literal: The chief ministers bowed their heads; all seated changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers bowed their heads; everyone present turned pale.

sentences.zh: 造徙坐從之，因曰：「陰陽不和，五谷踴貴，皆軍容事，宰相何與哉？

translations.literal: Zao moved his seat to follow and said: "Yin and yang are not in harmony, the five grains leap in price—all this is the Army Inspector's affair; what have the chief ministers to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Zao shifted his seat closer and said, "Yin and yang are out of balance and grain prices have soared—all matters of the Army Inspector. What have the chief ministers to do with it?

sentences.zh: 且軍挐不散，故天降之沴。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the armies are not dispersed, Heaven sends down calamity.
translations.idiomatic: And because the armies are not dispersed, Heaven sends down calamity.

sentences.zh: 今京師無事，六軍可相維鎮，又屯十萬，饋糧所以不足，百司無稍食，軍容為之，宰相行文書而已，何所歸罪？」

translations.literal: Now the capital is without incident; the Six Armies can mutually support and garrison it—yet another hundred thousand are encamped; therefore grain supplies are insufficient, the hundred offices have no stipends—the Army Inspector is responsible for this; the chief ministers merely transmit documents—upon what are they to be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: The capital is at peace; the Six Armies can garrison it together—yet another hundred thousand troops are encamped, grain supplies run short, and the hundred offices go without stipends. That is the Army Inspector's doing. The chief ministers merely transmit documents—why blame them?"

sentences.zh: 朝恩拂衣去，曰：「南衙朋黨，且害我。」

translations.literal: Chao'en brushed his robes and left, saying, "The southern yamen forms factions—they will yet harm me."
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en brushed off his robes and left, saying, "The southern yamen forms factions—they will yet destroy me."

sentences.zh: 會釋菜，執《易》升坐，百官鹹在，言《鼎》有覆餗象，以侵宰相。

translations.literal: At the ceremony of offering vegetables, he took up the Changes and ascended to the seat; all officials were present; he spoke of the Ding hexagram's image of overturned stew to attack the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the vegetable-offering ceremony he took up the Book of Changes and ascended to the seat. With all officials present, he spoke of the Ding hexagram's image of overturned stew to attack the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 王縉怒，元載怡然。

translations.literal: Wang Jin was angry; Yuan Zai was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin was furious; Yuan Zai remained calm.

sentences.zh: 朝恩曰：「怒者常情，笑者不可測也。」

translations.literal: Chao'en said, "Anger is a common emotion; the one who laughs cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en said, "Anger is common enough; the man who smiles is the one you cannot read."

sentences.zh: 載銜之未發。

translations.literal: Zai harbored resentment but did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Zai nursed a grudge but did not yet act.

sentences.zh: 朝恩有賜墅，觀沼勝爽，表為佛祠，為章敬太后薦福，即後謚以名祠，許之。

translations.literal: Chao'en had an imperial grant of a villa; its ponds and views were surpassingly fine; he memorialized to make it a Buddhist shrine to seek blessings for Empress Dowager Zhangjing—the shrine was later named after her posthumous title—and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en held an imperial grant of a villa with fine ponds and views. He memorialized to convert it into a Buddhist shrine to seek blessings for Empress Dowager Zhangjing. The shrine was later named for her posthumous title, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 於是用度侈浩，公壞曲江諸館、華清宮樓榭、百司行署、將相故第，收其材佐興作，費無慮萬億。

translations.literal: Thereupon expenditures were extravagant and vast; publicly they destroyed the various lodges at Qujiang, the towers and pavilions of Huaqing Palace, the offices of the hundred bureaus, and the former mansions of generals and chancellors, gathering their materials to assist construction; costs were reckoned in the trillions.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditures grew extravagant. Publicly they tore down the lodges at Qujiang, the towers of Huaqing Palace, government offices, and the former mansions of generals and chancellors, reusing the materials for construction. Costs ran into the trillions.

sentences.zh: 既數毀郭子儀，不見聽，乃遣盜發其先冢，子儀詭辭自解，以安眾疑。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly slandered Guo Ziyi without being heeded, he then sent thieves to open his ancestral tomb; Ziyi used evasive words to explain himself away and settle the public's suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated slanders against Guo Ziyi went unheeded, he sent thieves to rob Ziyi's ancestral tomb. Ziyi answered with evasive words to calm public suspicion.

sentences.zh: 久之，讓判國子監、鴻臚禮賓等使，加內侍監，徙封韓，增實封百戶。

translations.literal: After some time, he yielded administration of the Directorate of Education and the Court of Diplomatic Reception and Protocol Reception and other commissions, was given the additional post of Director of Palace Attendants, transferred his enfeoffment to Han, and had his substantive fief increased by a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he relinquished administration of the Directorate of Education and the courts of diplomatic and protocol reception, was promoted to Director of Palace Attendants, transferred his enfeoffment to Han, and received an increase of a hundred households to his substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 俄兼檢校國子監。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as acting administrator of the Directorate of Education.
