translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served concurrently as acting administrator of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 初，神策都虞候劉希暹魁健能騎射，最為朝恩昵信，以太仆卿封交河郡王。

translations.literal: At first, the Divine Strategy Army's chief adjutant Liu Xixuan was stalwart and strong, able in mounted archery, and most intimate and trusted by Chao'en; as Minister of the Stud he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaohe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Xixuan, chief adjutant of the Divine Strategy Army, was powerfully built and skilled in mounted archery. He was Chao'en's closest confidant and, as Minister of the Stud, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使王駕鶴獨謹厚，亦封徐國公。

translations.literal: The army horse commissioner Wang Jiahe alone was careful and generous, and was also enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The army horse commissioner Wang Jiahe alone was careful and generous, and was also enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 希暹諷朝恩置獄北軍，陰縱惡少年橫捕富人付吏考訊，因中以法，錄貲產入之軍，皆誣服冤死，故市人號「入地牢」。

translations.literal: Xixuan prompted Chao'en to establish a prison in the Northern Army; secretly he let wicked youths seize rich men by force and hand them to officials for interrogation, then fit them with the law, recorded their property and brought it into the army—all falsely confessed and died wrongfully; hence townspeople called it "entering the underground dungeon."
translations.idiomatic: Xixuan urged Chao'en to establish a prison in the Northern Army. Secretly he let ruffians seize wealthy men and hand them to officials for interrogation, then convict them by law, seize their property for the army, and send them to their deaths on false confessions. Townspeople called it "entering the underground dungeon."

sentences.zh: 又萬年吏賈明觀倚朝恩捕搏恣行，積財鉅萬，人無敢發其奸。

translations.literal: Also the Wanian clerk Jia Mingguan relied on Chao'en to arrest and plunder at will; he amassed wealth in the tens of thousands, and no one dared expose his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanian clerk Jia Mingguan also relied on Chao'en to arrest and plunder at will, amassing vast wealth, and no one dared expose his crimes.

sentences.zh: 朝廷裁決，朝恩或不預者，輒怒曰：「天下事有不由我乎！」

translations.literal: When the court rendered judgments in which Chao'en was sometimes not consulted, he would angrily say, "Are there affairs under Heaven that do not go through me!
translations.idiomatic: When the court rendered judgments without consulting him, he would angrily say, "Is there anything under Heaven that does not go through me!"

sentences.zh: 帝聞，不喜。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 養息令徽者，尚幼，為內給使，服綠，與同列爭忿，歸白朝恩。

translations.literal: There was Magistrate of Yangxi Ling Hui, still young, serving as an inner attendant in green robes; he quarreled with his peers in anger, returned and reported to Chao'en.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yangxi Ling Hui was still young and served as an inner attendant in green robes. After quarreling with his peers, he went to Chao'en to complain.

sentences.zh: 明日見帝曰：「臣之子位下，願得金紫，在班列上。」

translations.literal: The next day he saw the emperor and said, "Your subject's son holds a low position; he wishes to obtain gold and purple and stand in the ranks of court.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the emperor, "My son holds too low a rank. I wish him to receive gold and purple and stand in the court ranks."

sentences.zh: 帝未答，有司已奉紫服於前，令徽稱謝。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet replied when the relevant offices already presented purple robes before him and had Hui offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor could answer, the relevant offices had already presented purple robes and had Hui offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「小兒章服，大稱。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "A child's robes and insignia—a fine fit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Robes and insignia for a child—they fit him perfectly."

sentences.zh: 滋不悅。

translations.literal: Chao'en was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en was all the more displeased.

sentences.zh: 元載乃用左散騎常侍崔昭尹京兆，厚以財結其黨皇甫溫、周皓。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai then appointed Left Palace Attendant Cui Zhao as chief of Jingzhao, and lavishly used wealth to win over his factional allies Huangfu Wen and Zhou Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai then appointed Left Palace Attendant Cui Zhao to govern Jingzhao and used great wealth to win over his allies Huangfu Wen and Zhou Hao.

sentences.zh: 溫方屯陜，而皓射生將。

translations.literal: Wen was then stationed at Shanzhou, while Hao was a commander of the hunting guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was then garrisoned at Shanzhou, while Hao commanded the hunting guard.

sentences.zh: 自是朝恩隱謀奧語，悉為帝知。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chao'en's hidden schemes and secret counsels within the court all came to the emperor's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor learned of all Chao'en's hidden plots and secret counsels at court.

sentences.zh: 希暹覺帝指，密白朝恩，朝恩稍懼，然見帝接遇未衰，故自安而潛計不軌。

translations.literal: Xixuan perceived the emperor's intent and secretly reported to Chao'en. Chao'en grew somewhat fearful, yet seeing that the emperor's reception of him had not declined, he felt secure and secretly plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: Xixuan sensed the emperor's intent and secretly warned Chao'en. Chao'en grew somewhat afraid, but seeing that the emperor still treated him as before, he reassured himself and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝遂倚載決除之，懼不克，載曰：「陛下第專屬臣，必濟。」

translations.literal: The emperor then relied on Zai to decide on removing him, fearing failure. Zai said, "Your Majesty need only entrust the matter wholly to your subject—it will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then relied on Zai to decide how to remove him, fearing the attempt might fail. Zai said, "Your Majesty need only leave the matter entirely to me—it will succeed."

sentences.zh: 朝恩入殿，嘗從武士百人自衛，皓統之，而溫握兵在外。

translations.literal: When Chao'en entered the palace hall, he was accustomed to come with a hundred warrior guards under Hao's command, while Wen held troops outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao'en entered the palace, he habitually came escorted by a hundred warriors under Hao's command, while Wen held troops outside.

sentences.zh: 載乃徙鳳翔尹李抱玉節度山南西道，以溫代節度鳳翔，陽重其權，寔內溫以自助。

translations.literal: Zai then transferred Fengxiang prefect Li Baoyu to be military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, replacing Wen as military commissioner of Fengxiang—ostensibly to enhance Wen's authority, but in fact drawing Wen in to aid himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zai transferred Fengxiang prefect Li Baoyu to command Shannan West Circuit and had Wen replace him at Fengxiang, outwardly to enhance Wen's power but in fact to bring Wen in as his ally.

sentences.zh: 載又議析鳳翔之郿與京兆，以鄠、盩厔及鳳翔之虢、寶雞與抱玉，而以興平、武功、鳳翔之扶風天興與神策軍，朝恩利其土地，自封殖，不知為虞也。

translations.literal: Zai also proposed dividing Mei and Jingzhao from Fengxiang, assigning Hu, Zhouzhi, and Fengxiang's Guo and Baoji to Baoyu, while giving Xingping, Wugong, and Fengxiang's Fufeng and Tianxing to the Shence Army. Chao'en coveted the territory for his own enrichment and did not know he was being trapped.
translations.idiomatic: Zai also proposed splitting Mei and Jingzhao from Fengxiang, assigning Hu, Zhouzhi, and the Guo and Baoji districts of Fengxiang to Baoyu, while giving Xingping, Wugong, and Fufeng and Tianxing of Fengxiang to the Shence Army. Chao'en coveted the land for his own gain and did not realize he was walking into a trap.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀密白：「朝恩嘗結周智光為外應，久領內兵，不早圖，變且大。」

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi secretly reported, "Chao'en once allied with Zhou Zhiguang as an external ally. Having long commanded the inner army, if he is not dealt with early, the rebellion will be great.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi secretly warned the emperor, "Chao'en once allied with Zhou Zhiguang as an outside supporter. He has long commanded the inner army—if you do not move against him soon, the upheaval will be severe."

sentences.zh: 載留溫京師，未即遣，約與皓共誅朝恩。

translations.literal: Zai detained Wen in the capital and did not immediately dispatch him, arranging with Hao jointly to execute Chao'en.
translations.idiomatic: Zai kept Wen in the capital and did not send him out at once, arranging with Hao to kill Chao'en together.

sentences.zh: 謀定，以聞，帝曰：「善圖之，勿反受禍！」

translations.literal: When the plot was settled and reported, the emperor said, "Plan it well—do not instead suffer disaster!
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was set and reported, the emperor said, "Plan it carefully—do not bring disaster upon yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 方寒食，宴禁中，既罷，將還營，有詔留議事。

translations.literal: It was Cold Food Festival. After feasting in the palace, as Chao'en was about to return to camp, an edict ordered him detained for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: It was Cold Food Festival. After a feast in the palace, as Chao'en was about to return to camp, an edict ordered him to stay for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 朝恩素肥，每乘小車入宮省。

translations.literal: Chao'en had always been stout; each time he entered the palace precincts he rode in a small carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en had always been corpulent and entered the palace precincts each time in a small carriage.

sentences.zh: 帝聞車聲，危坐，載守中書省。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard the carriage sound, he sat upright in attention. Zai kept watch in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the carriage approach, the emperor sat bolt upright while Zai kept watch in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朝恩至，帝責其異圖，朝恩自辯悖傲，皓與左右禽縊之，死年四十九，外無知者。

translations.literal: When Chao'en arrived, the emperor rebuked him for his treacherous designs. Chao'en defended himself with perverse arrogance. Hao and attendants seized and strangled him. He died at forty-nine, and no one outside knew.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao'en arrived, the emperor rebuked him for treasonous designs. Chao'en answered with defiant arrogance. Hao and the attendants seized and strangled him. He was forty-nine; no one outside knew what had happened.

sentences.zh: 帝隱之，下詔罷觀軍容等使，增實封戶六百，內侍監如故。

translations.literal: The emperor kept it secret and issued an edict abolishing the post of army-observing commissioner, increasing his fief by six hundred households, while his office of Director of Palace Affairs remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the matter secret and issued an edict abolishing the army-observing commissionership, adding six hundred fief households, while leaving the office of Director of Palace Affairs unchanged.

sentences.zh: 外鹹言「既奉詔，乃投縊」雲。

translations.literal: Outside, all said, "Having received the edict, he then hanged himself," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the palace, everyone said, "After receiving the edict, he hanged himself."

sentences.zh: 還屍於家，賜錢六百萬以葬。

translations.literal: His corpse was returned to his home, and six million cash was granted for burial.
translations.idiomatic: His body was returned to his family, and six million cash was granted for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 帝懼軍亂，進劉希暹、王駕鶴並兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: The emperor feared military disorder and promoted Liu Xixuan and Wang Jihe, both concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing mutiny in the army, the emperor promoted Liu Xixuan and Wang Jihe, each concurrently to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 又下詔尉曉將士，獨希暹自知同惡，言不遜，駕鶴白髮之，遂賜死。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict to soothe the officers and men. Xixuan alone knew himself to be equally guilty; his words were insolent. Jihe reported his white hair, and he was then ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an edict to reassure the troops. Xixuan alone knew he shared in the guilt and spoke insolently. Jihe reported his white hair as proof of age, and he was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 而賈明觀兼得幸於載，故載奏隸江西，使立功自贖，路嗣恭搒殺之。

translations.literal: Jia Mingguan had also found favor with Zai, so Zai memorialized to assign him to Jiangxi to earn merit and redeem himself; Lu Sizong had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mingguan had also won Zai's favor, so Zai memorialized to assign him to Jiangxi to earn merit and redeem himself; Lu Sizong had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 所厚禮部尚書、禮儀使裴土淹、戶部侍郎判度支第五琦皆坐貶。

translations.literal: Pei Shiyan, Minister of Rites and Commissioner of Ceremonies, and Diwu Qi, Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently overseeing fiscal affairs, whom Chao'en had greatly favored, were both demoted on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shiyan, Minister of Rites and Commissioner of Ceremonies, and Diwu Qi, Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of fiscal affairs—both men Chao'en had favored—were demoted on account of the affair.

sentences.zh: 竇文場、霍仙鳴者，始並隸東宮，事德宗，未有名。

translations.literal: Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming had originally both served under the Eastern Palace and attended Dezong; they were not yet notable.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming had both originally served in the Eastern Palace under Dezong and were not yet well known.

sentences.zh: 自魚朝恩死，宦人不復典兵，帝以禁衛盡委白誌貞，誌貞多納富人金補軍，止收其庸而身不在軍。

translations.literal: After Yu Chao'en's death, eunuchs no longer commanded armies. The emperor entrusted the entire palace guard to Bai Zhizhen. Zhizhen took bribes from wealthy men to fill out the rolls, collecting only their service dues while the men themselves were not actually in the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Chao'en died, eunuchs no longer commanded troops. The emperor entrusted the entire palace guard to Bai Zhizhen, who took bribes from wealthy men to fill out the rolls, collecting only their service dues while they themselves never served.

sentences.zh: 及涇師亂，帝召近衛，無一人至者，惟文場等率宦官及親王左右從。

translations.literal: When the Jingzhou mutiny broke out, the emperor summoned the nearby guards, but not a single man came—only Wenchang and the others led eunuchs and attendants of princes to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhou mutiny broke out, the emperor summoned the nearby guards, but not one came—only Wenchang and the others led eunuchs and princes' attendants to follow him.

sentences.zh: 至奉天，帝逐誌貞，並左右軍付文場主之。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Fengtian, the emperor drove out Zhizhen and entrusted both the Left and Right Armies to Wenchang to administer.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian the emperor expelled Zhizhen and put both the Left and Right Armies under Wenchang's command.

sentences.zh: 興元初，詔監神策左廂兵馬，以王希遷監右，而馬有麟為左神策軍大將軍，軍額由此始。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, an edict appointed him to oversee the left wing troops of the Shence Army, with Wang Xiqian overseeing the right; Ma Youlin became Grand General of the Left Shence Army—from this the army designation began.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, an edict appointed him to oversee the left wing of the Shence Army, with Wang Xiqian overseeing the right; Ma Youlin became Grand General of the Left Shence Army—the army designation dates from this.

sentences.zh: 帝自山南還，兩軍復完，而帝忌宿將難制，故詔文場、仙鳴分總之，廢天威軍入左右神策。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from the south, both armies were restored to strength. The emperor feared that veteran generals would be hard to control, so he ordered Wenchang and Xianming each to command them jointly, incorporated the Tianwei Army into the Left and Right Shence, and dissolved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from the south, both armies were restored to full strength. Fearing that veteran generals would be hard to control, he had Wenchang and Xianming command them jointly and absorbed the Tianwei Army into the Left and Right Shence.

sentences.zh: 是時，竇、霍權振朝廷，諸方節度大將多出其軍，臺省要官走門下，丐援影者足相躡。

translations.literal: At this time Dou and Huo's power shook the court. Many frontier military commissioners and great generals came from their armies. High officials of the central ministries crowded their gates begging support and patronage, their footsteps treading on one another.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Dou and Huo's power shook the court. Many frontier commanders and great generals came from their armies. High officials of the central ministries crowded their gates seeking patronage, their footsteps treading on one another.

sentences.zh: 衛士朱華以按摩得幸文場，參慮補置，索賕數萬緡，而藩鎮贈遺累百鉅萬，略士妻女無所憚，詔殺之於軍。

translations.literal: Guard Zhu Hua, who had gained favor with Wenchang through massage, participated in deliberations on appointments, demanding bribes of tens of thousands of strings of cash. Military governors sent gifts totaling millions, and he seized commoners' wives and daughters without fear. An edict ordered him executed in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guard Zhu Hua won Wenchang's favor through massage and took part in deciding appointments, demanding bribes of tens of thousands of strings of cash. Military governors sent him gifts totaling millions, and he seized commoners' wives and daughters without fear. An edict ordered him executed in the army.

sentences.zh: 其隆赫如此。

translations.literal: Their splendor and dominance were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the height of their power and splendor.

sentences.zh: 久之，置護軍中尉、中護軍各二員，詔文場為左神策護軍中尉，仙鳴為右，焦希望為左神策中護軍，張尚進為右。

translations.literal: After some time, two Protectors of the Army and two Army Vice-Protectors were established. An edict appointed Wenchang Left Shence Protector of the Army, Xianming Right, Jiao Xiwang Left Shence Army Vice-Protector, and Zhang Shangjin Right.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, two Protectors of the Army and two Army Vice-Protectors were established. Wenchang was appointed Left Shence Protector of the Army, Xianming Right, Jiao Xiwang Left Shence Army Vice-Protector, and Zhang Shangjin Right.

sentences.zh: 中尉、護軍自文場等始。

translations.literal: The posts of Protector and Vice-Protector began with Wenchang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The posts of Protector and Vice-Protector began with Wenchang and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 後仙鳴移病，帝賜十馬，令諸祠祈解。

translations.literal: Later Xianming fell ill. The emperor granted ten horses and ordered prayers at various shrines for his recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xianming fell ill. The emperor granted ten horses and ordered prayers at shrines for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 後稍愈，已而暴死，帝疑左右進毒，捕詰小使問狀，誅數十人，贈開府儀同三司，以內常侍第五守亮代之。

translations.literal: He recovered somewhat, then suddenly died. The emperor suspected attendants had administered poison, arrested and interrogated junior servants, and executed several dozen. Xianming was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with identical ceremonial to the Three Dukes. Inner Palace Attendant Diwu Shouliang replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered somewhat, then suddenly died. The emperor suspected attendants had poisoned him, arrested and interrogated junior servants, and executed several dozen. Xianming was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes. Inner Palace Attendant Diwu Shouliang replaced him.

sentences.zh: 文場擢累驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Wenchang was promoted repeatedly to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang was promoted repeatedly until he reached General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史崔行囚於軍，吏為具酒食，欲悅媚之，故不拒。

translations.literal: At the time Investigating Censor Cui Xing was imprisoned in the army. An officer prepared wine and food hoping to please him, and he did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Investigating Censor Cui Xing was imprisoned in the army. An officer prepared wine and food to please him, and he did not refuse.

sentences.zh: 文場劾奏，詔流遠方。

translations.literal: Wenchang impeached and memorialized; an edict banished him to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang impeached him, and an edict banished him to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 文場年老致仕卒。

translations.literal: Wenchang retired in old age and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang retired in old age and later died.

sentences.zh: 其後楊誌廉、孫榮義為左右中尉，招權驕肆，與竇、霍略等。

translations.literal: Thereafter Yang Zhilian and Sun Rongyi served as Left and Right Protectors, monopolizing power with arrogant license, comparable to Dou and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Yang Zhilian and Sun Rongyi served as Left and Right Protectors, monopolizing power with arrogant license much like Dou and Huo.

sentences.zh: 帝晚節聞民間訛語禁中事，而北軍捕太學生何竦、曹壽系訊，人情大懼，司業武少儀上書「有如罪不測，願明示四方」。

translations.literal: In his late years the emperor heard popular rumors about affairs within the palace. The Northern Army arrested Imperial College students He Song and Cao Shou for interrogation. Public sentiment was greatly fearful. Vice Director Wu Shaoyi memorialized, "If there is offense beyond reckoning, I pray you make it clear to all the realm."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor heard popular rumors about palace affairs. The Northern Army arrested Imperial College students He Song and Cao Shou for interrogation, and public fear ran high. Vice Director Wu Shaoyi memorialized, "If the offense is unclear, I pray you make the truth known to all the realm."

sentences.zh: 俄得釋。

translations.literal: Soon they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were released.

sentences.zh: 是時宦官復盛矣。

translations.literal: At this time eunuch power flourished once again.
translations.idiomatic: At this time eunuch power was on the rise once again.

sentences.zh: 希望者，涇陽人，歷明威將軍，贈洪州都督。

translations.literal: Xiwang was a man of Jingyang. He held the rank of General of Illustrious Martiality and was posthumously granted Governor of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwang was a native of Jingyang. He rose to General of Illustrious Martiality and was posthumously granted Governor of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尚進，河東人，歷忠武將軍，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shangjin was a man of Hedong. He held the rank of General of Loyal Martiality and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with identical ceremonial to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjin was a native of Hedong. He rose to General of Loyal Martiality and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 誌廉，弘農人，歷左監門衛大將軍；

translations.literal: Zhiliang was a man of Hongnong. He held the rank of Grand General of the Left Gate Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiliang was a native of Hongnong and rose to Grand General of the Left Gate Guard;

sentences.zh: 榮義，涇陽人，歷右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Rongyi was a man of Jingyang. He held the rank of Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Rongyi was a native of Jingyang and rose to Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 並贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: All were posthumously granted Governor-General of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: All were posthumously granted Governor-General of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉貞亮，本俱氏，名文珍，冒所養宦父，故改焉。

translations.literal: Liu Zhenliang—originally of the Ju clan, named Wenzhen—usurped the surname of the eunuch who had raised him and therefore changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenliang was originally of the Ju clan and named Wenzhen; he took the surname of the eunuch who had raised him and therefore changed his name.

sentences.zh: 性忠強，識義理。

translations.literal: By nature he was loyal and firm; he understood right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was loyal and resolute and understood right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 平涼之盟，在渾瑊軍中，會虜變，被執且西，俄而得歸。

translations.literal: At the Pingliang alliance he was in Hun Zai's army. When the barbarians mutinied he was seized and taken west; soon he returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pingliang alliance he was in Hun Zai's army. When the barbarians mutinied he was captured and taken west, but soon returned.

sentences.zh: 出監宣武軍，自置親兵千人。

translations.literal: Sent out as army monitor of Xuanwu, he personally established a personal guard of a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as army monitor of Xuanwu, he personally raised a personal guard of a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，宦人領兵附順者益眾。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, eunuchs leading troops in obedient posts grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhenyuan era, eunuchs commanding troops in compliant posts had grown ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 會順宗立，淹痼弗能朝，惟李忠言、牛美人侍。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, he was long bedridden and unable to hold court; only Li Zhongyan and Niu Meiren attended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended the throne, he was long bedridden and unable to hold court; only Li Zhongyan and Niu Meiren attended him.

sentences.zh: 美人以帝旨付忠言，忠言授之王叔文，叔文與柳宗元等裁定，然後下中書。

translations.literal: Meiren entrusted the emperor's directives to Zhongyan, who passed them to Wang Shuwen; Shuwen together with Liu Zongyuan and others settled the matters, after which they were sent down to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Meiren passed the emperor's directives to Zhongyan, who handed them to Wang Shuwen; Shuwen together with Liu Zongyuan and others settled the matters before sending them to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 然未得縱欲，遂奪神策兵以自強，即用範希朝為京西北禁軍都將，收宦者權。

translations.literal: Yet they could not indulge their desires as they wished, so they seized the Shence troops to strengthen themselves, immediately appointing Fan Xichao as commander-in-chief of the capital northwest guard army, and reclaimed eunuch power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they could not indulge their desires as they wished, so they seized the Shence troops to strengthen themselves, immediately appointing Fan Xichao commander-in-chief of the capital northwest guard army and reclaiming power from the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 而忠言素懦謹，每見叔文與論事，無敢異同，唯貞亮乃與之爭。

translations.literal: But Zhongyan had always been timid and careful. Each time he saw Shuwen and discussed affairs he dared not disagree; only Zhenliang would contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhongyan had always been timid and cautious. Whenever he met with Shuwen to discuss affairs he dared not disagree; only Zhenliang would argue with him.

sentences.zh: 又惡朋黨熾結，因與中人劉光琦、薛文珍、尚衍、解玉、呂如全等同勸帝立廣陵王為太子監國，帝納其奏，貞亮召學士衛次公、鄭絪、李程、王涯至金鑾殿草定制詔。

translations.literal: He also hated that cliques were forming thick bonds, and together with fellow eunuchs Liu Guangqi, Xue Wenzhen, Shang Yan, Xie Yu, and Lü Ruquan persuaded the emperor to install the Prince of Guangling as heir apparent to oversee the realm. The emperor accepted their memorial. Zhenliang summoned Academicians Wei Cigong, Zheng Yu, Li Cheng, and Wang Ya to the Golden Lock Hall to draft the installing edict.
translations.idiomatic: He also hated the thickening of factional bonds and, together with fellow eunuchs Liu Guangqi, Xue Wenzhen, Shang Yan, Xie Yu, and Lü Ruquan, persuaded the emperor to install the Prince of Guangling as heir apparent to oversee the realm. The emperor accepted their memorial. Zhenliang summoned Academicians Wei Cigong, Zheng Yu, Li Cheng, and Wang Ya to the Golden Lock Hall to draft the installing edict.

sentences.zh: 太子已立，盡逐叔文黨，委政大臣，議者美其忠。

translations.literal: Once the heir apparent was installed, they drove out the entire Shuwen faction and entrusted governance to the chief ministers. Commentators praised Zhenliang's loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir apparent was installed, they drove out the entire Shuwen faction and entrusted governance to the chief ministers. Commentators praised Zhenliang's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 高崇文討劉辟，復為監軍。

translations.literal: When Gao Chongwen campaigned against Liu Pi, Zhenliang again served as army monitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Chongwen campaigned against Liu Pi, Zhenliang again served as army monitor.

sentences.zh: 初，東川節度使李康為辟所破，囚之。

translations.literal: Initially, Dongchuan military commissioner Li Kang had been defeated by Pi and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Dongchuan military commissioner Li Kang had been defeated by Pi and taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 崇文至，辟歸康求雪，貞亮劾以不拒賊，斬之，故以專悍見訾。

translations.literal: When Chongwen arrived, Pi returned Kang and sought absolution. Zhenliang impeached Kang for not resisting the rebel and had him executed—hence he was criticized as arbitrary and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongwen arrived, Pi returned Kang and sought absolution. Zhenliang impeached Kang for failing to resist the rebel and had him executed—hence he was criticized as arbitrary and harsh.

sentences.zh: 遷累右衛大將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand General of the Right Guard and Administrator of the Directorate of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand General of the Right Guard and put in charge of the Directorate of Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元和八年卒，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he died, and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with identical ceremonial to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Yuanhe and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之立，貞亮為有功，然終身無所寵假。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's installation, Zhenliang had merit, yet throughout his life he received no special favor or indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenliang had merit in Xianzong's accession, yet throughout his life he received no special favor or indulgence.

sentences.zh: 呂如全歷內侍省內常侍、翰林使，坐擅取樟材治第，送東都獄，至閿鄉自殺。

translations.literal: Lü Ruquan rose through Inner Palace Attendant and Hanlin Emissary. He was punished for seizing camphor timber to build a mansion and was sent to the eastern capital prison; at Wenxiang he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ruquan rose through Inner Palace Attendant and Hanlin Emissary. He was punished for seizing camphor timber to build a mansion and was sent to prison in the eastern capital; at Wenxiang he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 又郭旻醉觸夜禁，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Also Guo Min, drunk, violated the nighttime curfew and was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Min, drunk, violated the nighttime curfew and was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 五坊朱超晏、王誌忠縱鷹人入民家，搒二百，奪職，由是莫不懾畏。

translations.literal: The falconers Zhu Chaoyan and Wang Zhizhong of the Five Wards let their hawk handlers enter commoners' homes; they were beaten two hundred strokes and stripped of office—whereupon none failed to tremble in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The falconers Zhu Chaoyan and Wang Zhizhong of the Five Wards let their hawk handlers enter commoners' homes; they were beaten two hundred strokes and stripped of office—whereupon none failed to tremble in fear.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀，字仁貞，閩人也。

translations.literal: Tu Tu Chenghui, courtesy name Renzhen, was a man of Min.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Tu Chenghui, courtesy name Renzhen, was a native of Min.

sentences.zh: 以黃門直東宮，為掖廷局博士，察察有才。

translations.literal: As Yellow Gate attendant in the Eastern Palace he served as Erudit of the Inner Palace Department; he was sharp-eyed and talented.
translations.idiomatic: As a Yellow Gate attendant in the Eastern Palace he served as Erudit of the Inner Palace Department; he was sharp-eyed and talented.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，擢累左監門將軍、左神策護軍中尉、左街功德使，封薊國公。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended he was promoted repeatedly to General of the Left Gate Guard, Left Shence Protector of the Army, Commissioner of the Left Street Merit Hall, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne he was promoted repeatedly to General of the Left Gate Guard, Left Shence Protector of the Army, and Commissioner of the Left Street Merit Hall, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 王承宗叛，承璀揣帝銳征討，因請行。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Chenghui surmised that the emperor was eager to campaign and therefore requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Chenghui guessed that the emperor was eager to campaign and therefore volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 帝見其果敢，自喜，謂可任，即詔承璀為行營招討處置使，以左右神策及河中、河南、浙西、宣歙兵從之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw his boldness and was pleased, thinking him fit for the task. He immediately issued an edict appointing Chenghui Campaigning Commander and Disposal Commissioner, with the Left and Right Shence armies and troops from Hedong, Henan, Zhexii, and Xuanshe following him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his boldness and was pleased, thinking him fit for the task. He immediately appointed Chenghui Campaigning Commander and Disposal Commissioner, with the Left and Right Shence armies and troops from Hedong, Henan, Zhexii, and Xuanshe to follow him.

sentences.zh: 內寺伯宋惟澄、曹進玉為館驛使：自河南、陜、河陽，惟澄主之；

translations.literal: Inner Palace Herald Song Weicheng and Cao Jinyu served as courier commissioners: from Henan, Shan, and Heyang, Weicheng was in charge;
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Herald Song Weicheng and Cao Jinyu served as courier commissioners: from Henan, Shan, and Heyang, Weicheng was in charge;

sentences.zh: 京、華、河中至太原，進玉主之。

translations.literal: from the capital, Hua, and Hedong to Taiyuan, Jinyu was in charge.
translations.idiomatic: from the capital, Hua, and Hedong to Taiyuan, Jinyu was in charge.

sentences.zh: 又詔內常侍劉國珍、馬朝江分領易、定、幽、滄等州糧料使。

translations.literal: An edict also appointed Inner Palace Attendants Liu Guozhen and Ma Chaojiang to divide leadership of the grain commissioners for Yi, Ding, You, and Cang prefectures and others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also appointed Inner Palace Attendants Liu Guozhen and Ma Chaojiang to divide command of the grain commissioners for Yi, Ding, You, Cang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 於是諫官李鄘、許孟容、李元素、李夷簡、呂元膺、穆質、孟簡、獨孤郁、段平仲、白居易等眾對延英，謂古無中人位大帥，恐為四方笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon remonstrating officials Li Jiang, Xu Mengrong, Li Yuansu, Li Yijian, Lü Yuanying, Mu Zhi, Meng Jian, Dugu Yu, Duan Pingzhong, Bai Juyi, and others together faced the emperor in the Yanying Hall and said that in antiquity no eunuch held the rank of a great commander, fearing that the four quarters would laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon remonstrating officials Li Jiang, Xu Mengrong, Li Yuansu, Li Yijian, Lü Yuanying, Mu Zhi, Meng Jian, Dugu Yu, Duan Pingzhong, Bai Juyi, and others together faced the emperor in the Yanying Hall and said that in antiquity no eunuch had held the rank of a great commander, fearing the realm would laugh.

sentences.zh: 帝乃更為招討宣慰使，為禦通化門慰其行。

translations.literal: The emperor then changed the title to Campaigning Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner, and went to the Tonghua Gate to comfort him on his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then changed the title to Campaigning Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner and went to the Tonghua Gate to see him off.

sentences.zh: 承璀禦眾無它遠略，為盧從史侮狎，逾年無功，賴中詔擿使執從史，而間遣人說承宗上書待罪，乃詔班師，還為中尉。

translations.literal: Chenghui commanded the host without any far-reaching strategy. Lu Congshi treated him with contempt. More than a year passed without achievement. They relied on a secret imperial rescript to summon and seize Congshi, while intermittently sending men to persuade Chengzong to submit a memorial admitting guilt. Then an edict ordered withdrawal of troops. Chenghui returned as Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui commanded the army without any far-reaching strategy. Lu Congshi treated him with contempt. More than a year passed without success. They relied on a secret imperial rescript to summon and seize Congshi, while intermittently sending men to persuade Chengzong to submit a memorial admitting guilt. Then an edict ordered withdrawal. Chenghui returned as Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 平仲劾承璀輕謀弊賦，損國威，不斬首無以謝天下。

translations.literal: Pingzhong impeached Chenghui for rash planning that wasted the treasury and damaged national prestige, saying that unless his head were cut off there would be no way to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong impeached Chenghui for rash planning that wasted the treasury and damaged national prestige, saying that unless he were executed there would be no way to answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝不獲已，罷為軍器莊宅使。

translations.literal: The emperor, unable to refuse, demoted him to Commissioner of the Arsenal and Manorial Estates.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, the emperor demoted him to Commissioner of the Arsenal and Manorial Estates.

sentences.zh: 尋拜左衛上將軍，知內侍省。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Guard Senior General and Administrator of the Directorate of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Left Guard Senior General and put in charge of the Directorate of Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會劉希光納羽林大將軍孫璹錢二十萬緡求方鎮，有詔賜死，跡絓承璀，故令出監淮南軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Xiguang accepted two hundred thousand strings of cash from Feathered Forest Grand General Sun Zuan in exchange for a frontier command, an edict ordered Xiguang to die. Traces implicated Chenghui, so Chenghui was sent out to monitor the Huainan army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiguang accepted two hundred thousand strings of cash from Feathered Forest Grand General Sun Zuan in exchange for a frontier command, an edict ordered Xiguang to die. Traces implicated Chenghui, so Chenghui was sent out to monitor the Huainan army.

sentences.zh: 纖人太子通事舍人李涉投匭言承璀等冤狀，於是孔戣知匭事，閱其副，不受，即表其奸，逐為峽州司倉參軍。

translations.literal: Slanderer Li She, Attendant Master of Ceremonies to the Heir Apparent, submitted a petition-box memorial on Chenghui's and others' grievances. Kong Kai, in charge of the petition box, read the duplicate, refused to accept it, immediately memorialized exposing his treachery, and had him banished to be Storage Officer of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li She, Attendant Master of Ceremonies to the Heir Apparent, submitted a petition-box memorial on Chenghui's and others' grievances. Kong Kai, in charge of the petition box, read the duplicate, refused to accept it, immediately memorialized exposing his treachery, and had him banished to be Storage Officer of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 然帝於承璀殊厚，會李絳在翰林，苦論其過，故決遣之。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor was exceptionally generous toward Chenghui. When Li Jiang was in the Hanlin Academy and spoke bitterly of his faults, the emperor therefore decided to dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was exceptionally fond of Chenghui. When Li Jiang was in the Hanlin Academy and spoke bitterly of his faults, the emperor therefore decided to send him away.

sentences.zh: 帝後欲還承璀，為罷絳宰相，召為內弓箭庫使，復左神策中尉。

translations.literal: Later the emperor wished to recall Chenghui and dismissed Jiang from the chancellorship, recalled Chenghui as Inner Bow-and-Arrow Store Commissioner and restored him as Left Shence Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor wished to recall Chenghui, dismissed Jiang from the chancellorship, recalled Chenghui as Inner Bow-and-Arrow Store Commissioner, and restored him as Left Shence Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 惠昭太子薨，承璀請立澧王，不從。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Huizhao died, Chenghui requested that Li Li be installed as heir; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Huizhao died, Chenghui requested that the Prince of Li be installed as heir; the emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 常飾一室藏所賜詔敕，地生毛二尺，惡之，躬糞除瘞之。

translations.literal: He regularly adorned a room to store the edicts and orders he had received. The ground grew hair two feet long. He regarded it as ill-omened, personally swept manure and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a room adorned to store the edicts and orders he had received. The ground sprouted hair two feet long. He regarded it as an ill omen, personally cleared away the filth and buried it.

sentences.zh: 逾年帝崩，穆宗銜前議，殺之禁中。

translations.literal: More than a year later the emperor died. Muzong harbored resentment over the earlier dispute and had him killed within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the emperor died. Muzong harbored resentment over the earlier dispute and had him killed in the palace.

sentences.zh: 敬宗時，左神策中尉馬存亮論其冤，詔許子士曄收葬。

translations.literal: During Jingzong's reign, Left Shence Protector Ma Cunliang argued his innocence. An edict permitted his son Shi Ye to recover the body for burial.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingzong's reign, Left Shence Protector Ma Cunliang argued his innocence. An edict permitted his son Shi Ye to recover the body for burial.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，擢士曄右神策中尉。

translations.literal: During Xuanzong's reign, Shi Ye was promoted to Right Shence Protector.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuanzong's reign, Shi Ye was promoted to Right Shence Protector.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道歲進閹兒，號「私白」，閩、嶺最多，後皆任事，當時謂閩為中官區藪。

translations.literal: At this time each circuit annually presented castrated boys, called "private whites." Min and Ling regions sent the most. Later all held office. People at the time called Min a breeding ground for palace officials.
translations.idiomatic: At this time each circuit annually presented castrated boys, called "private whites." Min and the Ling region sent the most. Later all held office. People at the time called Min a breeding ground for palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，杜宣猷為觀察使，每歲時遣吏致祭其先，時號「敕使墓戶」。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era, Du Xuanyou was military commissioner. Each year at the proper seasons he sent officials to offer sacrifices at his ancestors' tombs. At the time he was called "the edict-commissioner's grave patron."
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era, Du Xuanyou served as observer. Each year at the proper seasons he sent officials to offer sacrifices at his ancestors' tombs. At the time he was called "the edict-commissioner's grave patron."

sentences.zh: 宣猷卒用群宦力徙宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: When Xuanyou died he used the collective power of the eunuchs to transfer to be observer of Xuanshe.
translations.idiomatic: Before his death Xuanyou used the collective power of the eunuchs to have himself transferred to observer of Xuanshe.

sentences.zh: 馬存亮，字季明，河中人。

translations.literal: Ma Cunliang, courtesy name Jiming, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Cunliang, courtesy name Jiming, was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 元和時，累擢左神策軍副使、左監門衛將軍，知內侍省事，進左神策中尉。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was promoted repeatedly to Deputy Commander of the Left Shence Army, General of the Left Gate Guard, Administrator of the Directorate of Palace Affairs, and advanced to Left Shence Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he was promoted repeatedly to Deputy Commander of the Left Shence Army, General of the Left Gate Guard, and Administrator of the Directorate of Palace Affairs, and advanced to Left Shence Protector.

sentences.zh: 軍所籍凡十餘萬，存亮料柬尤精，伍無罷士，部無冗員。

translations.literal: The rolls of the army totaled more than a hundred thousand. Cunliang's selection and organization were exceptionally meticulous; no squad had idle soldiers, no department had superfluous posts.
translations.idiomatic: The army rolls totaled more than a hundred thousand men. Cunliang's selection and organization were exceptionally meticulous: no squad had idle soldiers, no department had superfluous posts.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初，染署工張韶與卜者蘇玄明善，玄明曰：「我嘗為子卜，子當禦殿食，我與焉。

translations.literal: Early in Jingzong's reign, Dye Office craftsman Zhang Shao was on good terms with diviner Su Xuanming. Xuanming said, "I once divined for you—you shall eat in the imperial hall, and I shall be there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingzong's reign, Dye Office craftsman Zhang Shao was on good terms with diviner Su Xuanming. Xuanming said, "I once divined for you—you will dine in the imperial hall, and I will be there with you.

sentences.zh: 吾聞上晝夜獵，出入無度，可圖也。」

translations.literal: I hear that His Majesty hunts day and night, entering and leaving without restraint—a plot can be made.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Emperor hunts day and night, coming and going without restraint. He can be taken."

sentences.zh: 韶每輸染材入宮，衛士不呵也。

translations.literal: Shao regularly brought dye materials into the palace, and the guards did not challenge him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao regularly brought dye materials into the palace, and the guards never challenged him.

sentences.zh: 乃陰結諸工百餘人，匿兵車中若輸材者，入右銀臺門，約昏夜為變。

translations.literal: He then secretly gathered more than a hundred craftsmen, hid weapons in carts as though delivering materials, entered through the Right Yintai Gate, and arranged a coup for dusk.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly gathered more than a hundred craftsmen, concealed weapons in carts disguised as material deliveries, entered through the Right Yintai Gate, and set the uprising for dusk.

sentences.zh: 有詰其載者，韶謂謀覺，殺其人，出兵大呼成列，浴堂門閉。

translations.literal: When someone questioned his load, Shao thought the plot was discovered, killed the man, deployed troops shouting in formation; the Bath Hall gate was closed.
translations.idiomatic: When someone questioned his cargo, Shao thought the plot had been discovered, killed the man, deployed his armed men shouting as they formed ranks, and the Bath Hall gate was shut.

sentences.zh: 時帝擊球清思殿，驚，將幸右神策。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was playing cuju in Qingsi Hall, was alarmed, and was about to go to the Right Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was playing cuju in Qingsi Hall at the time. Alarmed, he prepared to flee to the Right Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「賊入宮，不知眾寡，道遠可虞，不如入左軍，近且速。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "The rebels have entered the palace; we do not know their numbers. The road is far and worrisome—better to enter the Left Army, which is near and quick.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "The rebels have entered the palace and we do not know how many they are. The route to the Right Army is long and risky—it would be better to go to the Left Army, which is close and quick."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: They followed this counsel.

sentences.zh: 初，帝常寵右軍中尉梁守謙，每遊幸；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had often favored Right Army Protector Liang Shouqian, taking him on every outing;
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Emperor had favored Right Army Protector Liang Shouqian, taking him along on every outing;

sentences.zh: 兩軍角戲，帝多欲右勝，而左軍以為望。

translations.literal: When the two armies competed in mock battle, the Emperor often wished the Right to win, and the Left Army felt disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: When the two armies staged mock battles, the Emperor often wanted the Right to win, leaving the Left Army disappointed.

sentences.zh: 至是，存亮出迎，捧帝足泣，負而入。

translations.literal: At this juncture Cunliang came out to meet him, clasped the Emperor's feet and wept, and carried him inside on his back.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Cunliang came out to meet him, clasped the Emperor's feet and wept, and carried him inside on his back.

sentences.zh: 以五百騎往迎二太后，比至，而賊已斬關入清思殿，升禦坐，盜乘輿餘膳，揖玄明偶食，且曰「如占」。

translations.literal: He sent five hundred horsemen to escort the two empress dowagers; by the time they arrived, the rebels had already forced the gates and entered Qingsi Hall, ascended the imperial throne, stole the Emperor's leftover meal, bowed to Xuanming to eat together, and said, "As the divination foretold."
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred horsemen were dispatched to escort the two empress dowagers; but by the time they arrived, the rebels had already broken through the gates into Qingsi Hall, ascended the imperial throne, stolen the Emperor's leftover meal, bowed to Xuanming to dine with him, and said, "Just as the divination foretold."

sentences.zh: 玄明驚曰：「止此乎！」

translations.literal: Xuanming exclaimed in alarm: "Is this all?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming cried out in alarm, "Is this all?"

sentences.zh: 韶惡之，悉以寶器賜其徒，攻弓箭庫，仗士拒之，不勝。

translations.literal: Shao hated this, distributed all precious vessels to his followers, attacked the bow-and-arrow storehouse; armed guards resisted them and they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Shao resented this, gave all the precious vessels to his followers, and attacked the bow-and-arrow storehouse; armed guards resisted and they could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 存亮遣左神策大將軍康藝全、將軍何文哲宋叔夜孟文亮，右神策大將軍康誌睦、將軍李泳尚國忠，率騎兵討賊，日暮，射韶及玄明皆死。

translations.literal: Cunliang sent Left Shence Grand General Kang Yiquan and Generals He Wenzhe, Song Shuye, and Meng Wenliang, and Right Shence Grand General Kang Zhimu and Generals Li Yong and Shang Guozhong, leading cavalry to suppress the rebels; at dusk they shot down Shao and Xuanming, both dead.
translations.idiomatic: Cunliang dispatched Left Shence Grand General Kang Yiquan and Generals He Wenzhe, Song Shuye, and Meng Wenliang, along with Right Shence Grand General Kang Zhimu and Generals Li Yong and Shang Guozhong, leading cavalry to suppress the rebels. At dusk they shot down Shao and Xuanming, killing them both.

sentences.zh: 始賊入，中人倉卒繇望仙門出奔，內外不知行在。

translations.literal: When the rebels first entered, inner eunuchs in haste fled out through Wangxian Gate; inside and outside did not know where the Emperor was.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first entered, palace eunuchs fled in haste through Wangxian Gate; inside and outside the palace, no one knew the Emperor's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 遲明，盡捕亂黨，左右軍清宮，車駕還。

translations.literal: At daybreak they captured all the rebels; the Left and Right armies cleared the palace, and the imperial carriage returned.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak all the rebels were captured; the Left and Right armies cleared the palace, and the Emperor returned.

sentences.zh: 群臣詣延英門見天子，然至者不十一二，坐賊所入闌不禁者數十人，杖而不誅，賜存亮實封戶二百，梁守謙進開府儀同三司，它論功賞有差。

translations.literal: The ministers went to Yan'ying Gate to see the Son of Heaven, yet those who arrived were not more than one or two in ten. Several dozen men were punished for having failed to bar the gate the rebels entered; they were caned but not executed. Cunliang was granted two hundred households in perpetual tax income; Liang Shouqian was promoted to Senior Grand Master of Splendid State with the status of the Three Excellencies; others were rewarded according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers went to Yan'ying Gate to see the Emperor, yet fewer than one or two in ten arrived. Several dozen men who had failed to bar the gate the rebels entered were caned but not executed. Cunliang was granted two hundred households of perpetual revenue; Liang Shouqian was promoted to Senior Grand Master of Splendid State with the ceremonial rank of the Three Excellencies; others were rewarded according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 存亮於一時功最高，乃推委權勢，求監淮南軍。

translations.literal: Cunliang's achievement at that moment was the highest, yet he yielded authority and power, and requested to supervise the Huainan army.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cunliang had earned the highest distinction in the crisis, he set aside authority and power and requested to supervise the Huainan army.

sentences.zh: 代還，為內飛龍使。

translations.literal: When his replacement returned, he became Inner Flying Dragon Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After his successor returned, he was appointed Inner Flying Dragon Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大和中，以右領軍衛上將軍致仕，封岐國公，卒贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era he retired as Senior General of the Right Imperial Guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and upon death was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe era he retired as Senior General of the Right Imperial Guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and upon death was posthumously given the title Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 存亮逮事德宗，更六朝，資端畏，善訓士，始去禁衛，眾皆泣。

translations.literal: Cunliang served as far back as Dezong, passing through six reigns; his nature was upright and cautious, skilled at training troops. When he first left the palace guard, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Cunliang had served since Dezong's reign, passing through six reigns. Upright and cautious by nature, he excelled at training soldiers. When he first departed the palace guard, all his men wept.

sentences.zh: 唐世中人以忠謹稱者，唯存亮、西門季玄、嚴遵美三人而已。

translations.literal: Among Tang-era palace eunuchs praised for loyalty and prudence, only Cunliang, Ximen Jixuan, and Yan Zunmei—these three alone.
translations.idiomatic: Among Tang-era eunuchs praised for loyalty and prudence, only Cunliang, Ximen Jixuan, and Yan Zunmei counted.

sentences.zh: 遵美父季寔，為掖廷局博士。

translations.literal: Zunmei's father Ji Shi was a doctor of the Yeting Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Zunmei's father, Ji Shi, served as a doctor of the Yeting Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大中時，有宮人謀弒宣宗。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era, a palace woman plotted to assassinate Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era, a palace woman plotted to assassinate Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 是夜，季寔直鹹寧門下，聞變，入射殺之。

translations.literal: That night Ji Shi was on duty below Xianning Gate; hearing of the disturbance, he entered and shot her dead.
translations.idiomatic: That night Ji Shi was on duty at Xianning Gate; hearing of the disturbance, he entered and shot her dead.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝勞曰：「非爾，吾危不免。」

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor commended him, saying: "Had it not been for you, I would scarcely have escaped danger.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor thanked him, saying, "Had it not been for you, I could not have escaped with my life."

sentences.zh: 擢北院副使，終內樞密使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court and ultimately became Director of the Inner Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court and ultimately rose to Director of the Inner Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 遵美歷左軍容使，嘗嘆曰：「北司供奉官以胯衫給事，今執笏，過矣。

translations.literal: Zunmei served as Left Army Aide Commissioner and once sighed, saying: "Northern Bureau attendants served in split-skirt robes; now they hold court tablets—this has gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: Zunmei served as Left Army Aide Commissioner. He once sighed and said, "Attendants of the Northern Bureau once served in split-skirt robes; now they hold court tablets—that has gone too far.

sentences.zh: 樞密使無聽事，唯三楹舍藏書而已，今堂狀帖黃決事，此楊復恭奪宰相權之失也。」

translations.literal: The Privy Council Commissioner had no audience hall, only a three-bay lodge for storing books; now they decide affairs with hall summaries and yellow slips—this was Yang Fugong's error in seizing the chancellor's power.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council Commissioner had no audience hall—only a three-bay lodge for storing books. Now they decide affairs through hall summaries and yellow slips pasted on memorials. This was the error Yang Fugong made when he usurped the chancellor's authority."

sentences.zh: 蓋疾時中官肆橫云。

translations.literal: —Thus he lamented the rampant arrogance of eunuchs of his day.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his lament at the rampant excess of eunuchs in his time.

sentences.zh: 後從昭宗遷鳳翔，求致仕，隱青城山，年八十餘卒。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Zhaozong's move to Fengxiang, requested retirement, retired to seclusion on Mount Qingcheng, and died in his eighties.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Zhaozong to Fengxiang, requested retirement, and withdrew to seclusion on Mount Qingcheng, where he died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 仇士良，字匡美，循州興寧人。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang, courtesy name Kuangmei, was a man of Xingning in Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang, courtesy name Kuangmei, was a native of Xingning in Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 順宗時得侍東宮。

translations.literal: During Shunzong's reign he came to serve the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Shunzong's reign he entered service in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，再遷內給事，出監平盧、鳳翔等軍。

translations.literal: When Xianzong succeeded to the throne, he was twice promoted to Inner Provisioner and sent out to supervise the Pinglu, Fengxiang, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong succeeded to the throne, he was promoted twice to Inner Provisioner and sent out to supervise the Pinglu, Fengxiang, and other armies.

sentences.zh: 嘗次敷水驛，與御史元稹爭舍上廳，擊傷稹。

translations.literal: He once stopped at Fushui Post Station and contended with Censor Yuan Zhen for the main hall lodging, striking and injuring Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while stopping at Fushui Post Station, he contended with Censor Yuan Zhen for the main hall and struck him, injuring him.

sentences.zh: 中丞王播奏御史、中使以先後至得正寢，請如舊章。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Bo memorialized that censors and inner commissioners should occupy the principal chamber according to who arrived first, requesting the old regulation be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Bo memorialized that censors and imperial commissioners should take the main lodging according to who arrived first, and asked that the old regulation be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝不直稹，斥其官。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not side with Zhen and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not support Zhen and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 元和、大和間，數任內外五坊使，秋按鷹內畿，所至邀吏供餉，暴甚寇盜。

translations.literal: Between the Yuanhe and Dahe eras he repeatedly served as Inner and Outer Commissioner of the Five Camps; in autumn he inspected hawks within the inner circuits, and wherever he went he pressed officials for supplies—his depredations exceeded those of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yuanhe and Dahe eras he repeatedly served as commissioner of the Five Camps, inspecting hawks within the capital region each autumn. Wherever he went he demanded supplies from officials, and his depredations surpassed those of bandits.

sentences.zh: 文宗與李訓欲殺王守澄，以士良素與守澄隙，故擢左神策軍中尉兼左街功德使，使相糜肉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong and Li Xun wished to kill Wang Shoucheng; because Shiliang had long been at odds with Shoucheng, they promoted him to Left Shence Army Protector and concurrently Left Street Merit Commissioner, to make them consume each other's flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong and Li Xun plotted to kill Wang Shoucheng. Because Shiliang had long been at odds with Shoucheng, they promoted Shiliang to Left Shence Army Protector and concurrent Left Street Merit Commissioner, setting the two against each other like wolves tearing each other's flesh.

sentences.zh: 已而訓謀悉逐中官，士良悟其謀，與右神策軍中尉魚弘誌、大盈庫使宋守義挾帝還宮。

translations.literal: Before long Xun plotted to expel all inner officials; Shiliang perceived the plot and, with Right Shence Army Protector Yu Hongzhi and Commissioner of the Great Abundance Storehouse Song Shouyi, seized the Emperor and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xun plotted to expel all eunuch officials. Shiliang saw through the scheme and, with Right Shence Army Protector Yu Hongzhi and Commissioner of the Great Abundance Storehouse Song Shouyi, seized the Emperor and carried him back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 王涯、舒元輿已就縛，士良肆脅辱，令自承反，示牒於朝。

translations.literal: Wang Ya and Shu Yuanyu were already bound; Shiliang wantonly threatened and humiliated them, forcing them to confess rebellion themselves, and displayed the documents at court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya and Shu Yuanyu were already bound. Shiliang wantonly threatened and humiliated them into confessing treason themselves, then displayed the confessions at court.

sentences.zh: 於時莫能辨其情，皆謂誠反，士良因縱兵捕，無輕重悉斃兩軍，公卿半空。

translations.literal: At the time none could discern the truth; all said they had truly rebelled. Shiliang therefore unleashed troops to seize people; without distinction of severity all were killed between the two armies, and the ranks of ministers and nobles were half emptied.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no one could discern the truth—all believed they had truly rebelled. Shiliang therefore unleashed his troops to seize whomever they could; without regard to guilt or innocence, countless people were killed between the two armies, and the ranks of ministers and nobles were decimated.

sentences.zh: 事平，加特進、右驍衛大將軍，弘誌右衛上將軍兼中尉，守義右領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was given the special advancement and made Grand General of the Right Martial Cavaliery; Hongzhi became Senior General of the Right Guard and concurrent Protector; Shouyi became Senior General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis was settled, Shiliang was given the special advancement and made Grand General of the Right Martial Cavaliery; Hongzhi became Senior General of the Right Guard and concurrent Protector; Shouyi became Senior General of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 李石輔政，棱棱有風岸，士良與論議數屈，深忌之，使賊刺石於親仁裏，馬逸而免。

translations.literal: When Li Shi assisted in governance, he was stern with imposing integrity; Shiliang was repeatedly bested in debates and deeply resented him; he sent assassins to stab Shi at Qinren Lane; his horse bolted and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shi served as chief minister, he was stern and upright. Shiliang was repeatedly bested in debate and deeply resented him; he sent assassins to ambush Shi in Qinren Lane, but Shi's horse bolted and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 石懼，辭位，士良益無憚。

translations.literal: Shi was afraid and resigned his post; Shiliang grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Shi resigned; Shiliang grew ever more unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 澤潞劉從諫本與訓約誅鄭註。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian of Zelu had originally conspired with Xun to execute Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian of Zelu had originally joined Xun in a pact to execute Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 及訓死，憤士良得誌，乃上書言：「王涯等八人皆宿儒大臣，願保富貴，何苦而反。

translations.literal: When Xun died, furious that Shiliang had gotten his way, he submitted a memorial saying: "Wang Ya and the other eight were all longstanding Confucian ministers who wished only to preserve their wealth and honors—why would they painfully rebel?
translations.idiomatic: When Xun died, enraged that Shiliang had gotten his way, Congjian submitted a memorial: "Wang Ya and the other eight were all long-serving Confucian ministers who wished only to preserve their wealth and status—why would they rebel at such cost?

sentences.zh: 今大戮所加已不可追，而名之逆賊，含憤九泉。

translations.literal: Now the mass execution already applied cannot be undone, yet they are named traitorous rebels—bearing resentment in the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: The mass execution can no longer be undone, yet they are branded traitorous rebels—they lie beneath the earth nursing their grievance.

sentences.zh: 不然，天下義夫節士，畏禍伏身，誰肯與陛下共治耶？」

translations.literal: If not, righteous men and men of integrity throughout the realm, fearing calamity and hiding themselves—who would be willing to govern together with Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If not, righteous men and men of integrity throughout the realm will fear disaster and hide themselves—who then will be willing to govern with Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 即以訓所移書遣部將陳季卿以聞。

translations.literal: He then sent the letter Xun had forwarded, dispatching his subordinate general Chen Jiqing to report it.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched his subordinate general Chen Jiqing to deliver the letter Xun had forwarded and report to the court.

sentences.zh: 季卿至，會石遇盜，京師擾，疑不敢進。

translations.literal: When Jiqing arrived, Li Shi encountered robbers and the capital was in turmoil; he doubted and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqing arrived, Li Shi had just survived an assassination attempt and the capital was in turmoil; suspicious and afraid, he did not dare present the memorial.

sentences.zh: 從諫大怒，殺季卿，騰書於朝。

translations.literal: Congjian flew into a rage, killed Jiqing, and posted the letter at court.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was furious, had Jiqing executed, and had the letter circulated openly at court.

sentences.zh: 又言：「臣與訓誅註，以註本宦豎所提挈，不使聞知。

translations.literal: He further stated: "Your subject and Xun executed Zhu because Zhu had been promoted by eunuchs—we did not let them know.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Your subject joined with Xun in executing Zhu because Zhu had been promoted by eunuchs—we kept them from knowing of it.

sentences.zh: 今四方共傳宰相欲除內官，而兩軍中尉聞，自救死，妄相殺戮，謂為反逆。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters jointly circulate word that the chancellor wished to remove inner officials; the two army Protectors heard, fought to save their own lives, wantonly slaughtered each other, and called it rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Now rumor spreads everywhere that the chancellor sought to remove eunuch officials; the two army Protectors heard of it, fought to save themselves, indiscriminately slaughtered people, and called it treason.

sentences.zh: 有如大臣挾無將之謀，自宜執付有司，安有縱俘劫、橫屍闕下哉？

translations.literal: If great ministers harbored treasonous designs, they should rightly be handed over to the appropriate offices—how could one unleash captive-soldier pillaging and leave corpses strewn below the palace gate?
translations.idiomatic: Had great ministers truly harbored treasonous designs, they should properly have been handed over to the judicial authorities—how could troops have been let loose to pillage and leave corpses strewn before the palace gates?

sentences.zh: 陛下視不及，聽未聞也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's eyes did not see, your ears did not hear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty neither saw nor heard.

sentences.zh: 且宦人根黨蔓延在內，臣欲面陳，恐橫遭戮害，謹修封疆，繕甲兵，為陛下腹心。

translations.literal: Moreover, eunuch factions spread their roots within; your subject wishes to speak face to face but fears being slaughtered on the spot; I therefore carefully secure my borders, repair armor and weapons, and serve as Your Majesty's trusted heart.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover eunuch factions spread their roots deep within the palace. Your subject wishes to speak to Your Majesty in person but fears being killed on the spot. I therefore secure my borders, repair armor and weapons, and stand as Your Majesty's loyal bulwark.

sentences.zh: 如奸臣難制，誓以死清君側。」

translations.literal: If treacherous ministers are hard to control, I swear to clear them from the sovereign's side even at the cost of my life.
translations.idiomatic: If treacherous ministers cannot be controlled, I swear to purge them from Your Majesty's side even at the cost of my life."

sentences.zh: 書聞，人人傳觀。

translations.literal: When the letter was received, everyone passed it around to read.
translations.idiomatic: When the letter reached the court, everyone circulated it to read.

sentences.zh: 士良沮恐，即進從諫檢校司徒，欲弭其言。

translations.literal: Shiliang was dejected and afraid; he immediately recommended Congjian as Acting Minister of Education, wishing to quiet his words.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was shaken with fear and immediately had Congjian appointed Acting Minister of Education, hoping to silence him.

sentences.zh: 從諫知可動，復言：「臣所陳系國大體，可聽，則宜洗宥涯等罪；

translations.literal: Congjian knew they could be moved and again stated: "What your subject has stated concerns the great principles of the state; if it may be heeded, then Wang Ya and the others' crimes should be cleared and pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they were wavering, Congjian wrote again: "What I have stated concerns the fundamental interests of the state. If Your Majesty will hear me, Wang Ya and the others' crimes should be cleared and pardoned;

sentences.zh: 不可聽，則賞不宜妄出。

translations.literal: if it may not be heeded, then rewards should not be issued recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: if not, rewards should not be dispensed heedlessly.

sentences.zh: 安有死冤不申，而生者荷祿？」

translations.literal: How can there be deaths with unredressed grievances while the living enjoy salaries?
translations.idiomatic: How can the dead lie with unredressed grievances while the living draw their salaries?"

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 累上書，暴指士良等罪。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials, openly indicting Shiliang and others' crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial, openly indicting the crimes of Shiliang and his allies.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能去，然倚其言差自強。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor could not remove them, relying on his words he grew somewhat stronger in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor could not remove Shiliang, he drew some strength from Congjian's words and grew somewhat firmer in resolve.

sentences.zh: 自是郁郁不樂，兩軍球獵宴會絕矣。

translations.literal: From then on the Emperor was depressed and unhappy; the two armies' cuju, hunting, and banquets ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Emperor grew melancholy and joyless, and the two armies' cuju, hunts, and banquets ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，苦風痹，少間，召宰相見延英，退坐思政殿，顧左右曰：「所直學士謂誰？」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng he suffered severely from wind paralysis; after a brief respite he summoned the chancellor to Yan'ying, then withdrew and sat in Sizheng Hall, turned to those beside him and said: "Who is the on-duty academician?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaicheng he was racked by rheumatism. After a brief respite he summoned the chancellor to Yan'ying Hall, then withdrew to Sizheng Hall and asked those beside him, "Who is the academician on duty today?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「周墀也。」

translations.literal: They said: "Zhou Chi."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Zhou Chi."

sentences.zh: 召至，帝曰：「自爾所況，朕何如主？」

translations.literal: He was summoned; the Emperor said: "From what you have observed, what kind of sovereign am I?"
translations.idiomatic: Chi was summoned. The Emperor said, "From what you have observed, what sort of ruler am I?"

sentences.zh: 墀再拜曰：「臣不足以知，然天下言陛下堯、舜主也。」

translations.literal: Chi bowed twice and said: "Your subject is not adequate to know, yet the realm says Your Majesty is a sovereign of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Chi bowed twice and said, "I am not qualified to judge, yet the realm calls Your Majesty a ruler in the mold of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「所以問，謂與周赧、漢獻孰愈？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The reason I ask is to compare with King Nan of Zhou and Emperor Xian of Han—which is better?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I ask because I wish to know—am I better or worse than King Nan of Zhou and Emperor Xian of Han?"

sentences.zh: 墀惶駭曰：「陛下之德，成、康、文、景未足比，何自方二主哉？」

translations.literal: Chi said in panic: "Your Majesty's virtue—Cheng, Kang, Wen, and Jing are not enough for comparison; why compare yourself to those two sovereigns?"
translations.idiomatic: Chi replied in alarm, "Your Majesty's virtue surpasses even the kings Cheng, Kang, Wen, and Jing—how could you compare yourself to those two?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「赧、獻受制強臣，今朕受制家奴，自以不及遠矣！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Nan and Xian were controlled by powerful ministers; now I am controlled by household slaves—I consider myself far inferior!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Nan and Xian were controlled by powerful ministers, but I am controlled by household slaves—I consider myself far beneath them!"

sentences.zh: 因泣下，墀伏地流涕。

translations.literal: He then wept; Chi prostrated himself and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke, and Chi prostrated himself, weeping.

sentences.zh: 後不復朝，至大漸雲。

translations.literal: Afterward he no longer held court; until his final illness, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he held court no more, until his final illness.

sentences.zh: 始，樞密使劉弘逸薛季棱、宰相李玨楊嗣復謀奉太子監國，士良與弘誌議更立，玨不從，乃矯詔立潁王為皇太弟，士良以兵奉迎，而太子還為陳王。

translations.literal: At first, Privy Envoys Liu Hongyi and Xue Jileng and chancellors Li Jue and Yang Sifu planned to have the crown prince supervise the state. Shiliang and Hongzhi discussed establishing someone else, but Jue would not agree. They then forged an edict making the Prince of Ying imperial younger brother, and Shiliang welcomed him with troops, while the crown prince was returned to being Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Privy Envoys Liu Hongyi and Xue Jileng and chancellors Li Jue and Yang Sifu planned to have the crown prince supervise the state. Shiliang and Hongzhi discussed establishing someone else, but Jue would not agree. They then forged an edict making the Prince of Ying imperial younger brother, and Shiliang welcomed him with troops, while the crown prince was returned to being Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 初，莊恪太子薨，楊賢妃謀引安王，不克。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Crown Prince Zhuangke died, Worthy Consort Yang had plotted to bring in the Prince of An but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Crown Prince Zhuangke died, Worthy Consort Yang had plotted to bring in the Prince of An but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 武宗已立，士良發其事，勸帝除之以絕人望，故王、妃皆死。

translations.literal: After Wuzong had been enthroned, Shiliang exposed the matter and urged the emperor to eliminate them in order to cut off people's hopes; therefore both the prince and the consort died.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuzong had been enthroned, Shiliang exposed the matter and urged the emperor to eliminate them in order to cut off people's hopes; therefore both the prince and the consort died.

sentences.zh: 士良遷驃騎大將軍，封楚國公，弘誌韓國公，實封戶三百。

translations.literal: Shiliang was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Chu; Hongzhi was made Duke of Han, with an actual fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Chu; Hongzhi was made Duke of Han, with an actual fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 俄而玨、嗣復罷去，弘逸、季棱誅矣。

translations.literal: Soon Jue and Sifu were removed from office, and Hongyi and Jileng were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jue and Sifu were removed from office, and Hongyi and Jileng were executed.

sentences.zh: 帝明斷，雖士良有援立功，內實嫌之，陽示尊寵。

translations.literal: The Emperor was clear and decisive; though Shiliang had aided him and achieved merit, inwardly he truly resented him and outwardly displayed honor and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was clear-minded and decisive. Though Shiliang had saved him and earned merit, he secretly resented him while outwardly showering him with honor.

sentences.zh: 李德裕得君，士良愈恐。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu won the sovereign's trust, Shiliang grew ever more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu gained the Emperor's confidence, Shiliang grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，上尊號，士良宣言「宰相作赦書，減禁軍縑糧芻菽」以搖怨，語兩軍曰：「審有是，樓前可爭。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang, when the honorific title was conferred, Shiliang proclaimed that "the chancellor wrote the amnesty edict, reducing forbidden-army silk rations and fodder" to stir resentment, saying to the two armies: "If this is so, you may protest before the tower."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huichang, during the conferral of the honorific title, Shiliang spread word that "the chancellor wrote the amnesty edict cutting the forbidden army's silk rations and fodder" to stir up resentment, telling the two armies, "If this is true, you may protest before the palace tower."

sentences.zh: 德裕以白帝，命使者諭神策軍曰：「赦令自朕意，宰相何豫？

translations.literal: Deyu reported to the Emperor, who ordered an envoy to instruct the Shence Army: "The amnesty issued from my intent—what has the chancellor to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Deyu reported this to the Emperor, who sent an envoy to instruct the Shence Army, "The amnesty came from my own intent—what business is it of the chancellor's?

sentences.zh: 爾渠敢是？」

translations.literal: Do you lot dare this?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you lot do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 士乃怗然。

translations.literal: The soldiers then grew quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers then quieted down.

sentences.zh: 士良惶惑不自安。

translations.literal: Shiliang was alarmed and unsettled, ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was shaken and ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 明年，進觀軍容使，兼統左右軍，以疾辭，罷為內侍監，知省事。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to Military Observation Commissioner and given concurrent command of both armies; citing illness he resigned, was dismissed to Palace Attendant Supervisor, administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Military Observation Commissioner with concurrent command of both armies; citing illness he resigned and was reduced to Palace Attendant Supervisor, administering routine affairs.

sentences.zh: 固請老，詔可。

translations.literal: He firmly requested to retire on account of age; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly requested retirement on account of age; the Emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Soon he died; posthumously granted Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously given the title Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 士良之老，中人舉送還第，謝曰：「諸君善事天子，能聽老夫語乎？」

translations.literal: When Shiliang retired, eunuchs escorted him home in a procession; he thanked them, saying: "Gentlemen, serve the Son of Heaven well—will you listen to this old man's words?
translations.idiomatic: When Shiliang retired, fellow eunuchs escorted him home in procession. He addressed them: "Serve the Son of Heaven well—will you heed an old man's counsel?"

sentences.zh: 眾唯唯。

translations.literal: The crowd murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 士良曰：「天子不可令閑暇，暇必觀書，見儒臣，則又納諫，智深慮遠，減玩好，省遊幸，吾屬恩且薄而權輕矣。

translations.literal: Shiliang said: "The Son of Heaven must not be allowed leisure; in leisure he inevitably reads books, sees Confucian officials, and then accepts remonstrance—deep in wisdom, far in forethought, reducing playthings, curtailing excursions—our kind's favor will thin and our power lighten.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang said, "The Son of Heaven must never be allowed idle hours. In idleness he will read books, receive Confucian ministers, and accept remonstrance—growing wise and far-sighted, cutting back diversions and curtailing excursions—and then our favor will wane and our power shrink.

sentences.zh: 為諸君計，莫若殖財貨，盛鷹馬，日以球獵聲色蠱其心，極侈靡，使悅不知息，則必斥經術，阇外事，萬機在我，恩澤權力欲焉往哉？」

translations.literal: For your sake, gentlemen, none surpasses amassing wealth and goods, maintaining hawks and horses, daily filling his heart with cuju, hunting, music, and women, to the utmost extravagance, making him pleased and unknowing of rest—then he will certainly dismiss the classics, block out external affairs; the myriad responsibilities will be in our hands—where will favor, grace, and power go?
translations.idiomatic: For your own sakes, nothing surpasses amassing wealth, keeping fine hawks and horses, and daily filling the Emperor's heart with cuju, hunts, music, and women—extravagance without limit, pleasure without cease—until he dismisses the classics, shuts out affairs of state, and the myriad responsibilities fall into our hands. Then where will favor, grace, and power go but to us?"

sentences.zh: 眾再拜。
