translations.literal: The crowd bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd bowed twice in assent.

sentences.zh: 士良殺二王、一妃、四宰相，貪酷二十餘年，亦有術自將，恩禮不衰雲。

translations.literal: Shiliang killed two princes, one consort, and four chancellors; greedy and cruel for more than twenty years, yet he also had the art of self-management—the text says his favor and courtesy never waned.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang killed two princes, one consort, and four chancellors. Greedy and ruthless for more than twenty years, he nevertheless knew how to manage himself—so the text says his favor and standing never waned.

sentences.zh: 死之明年，有發其家藏兵數千物，詔削官爵，籍其家。

translations.literal: The year after his death, weapons numbering in the thousands were discovered in his home; an edict stripped his titles and registered his property for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: The year after his death, thousands of weapons were discovered hidden in his home; an edict stripped his titles and confiscated his estate.

sentences.zh: 始，士良、弘誌憤文宗與李訓謀，屢欲廢帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Shiliang and Hongzhi were angry that Wenzong had conspired with Li Xun and repeatedly wished to depose the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Shiliang and Hongzhi, furious that Wenzong had conspired with Li Xun, repeatedly sought to depose the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 崔慎由為翰林學士，直夜未半，有中使召入，至秘殿，見士良等坐堂上，帷帳周密，謂慎由曰：「上不豫已久，自即位，政令多荒闕，皇太后有制更立嗣君，學士當作詔。」

translations.literal: Cui Shenyou was a Hanlin academician; past midnight on his night duty, an inner commissioner summoned him; he reached the secret hall and saw Shiliang and others seated in the hall; the curtains were closely drawn; they said to Shenyou: "His Majesty has been unwell for a long time; since ascending the throne, government orders have been largely neglected; the empress dowager has issued orders to install a new heir—Academician, you must draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Cui Shenyou was on night duty past midnight when an inner commissioner summoned him to a secret hall, where Shiliang and others sat with curtains drawn tight. They told Shenyou, "The Emperor has long been unwell; since his accession government has been largely neglected. The empress dowager has issued orders to install a new heir—you must draft the edict."

sentences.zh: 慎由驚曰：「上高明之德在天下，安可輕議？

translations.literal: Shenyou said in alarm: "His Majesty's enlightened virtue is known throughout the realm—how may this be lightly discussed?
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou exclaimed in alarm, "The Emperor's enlightened virtue is known throughout the realm—how can such a thing be lightly discussed?

sentences.zh: 慎由親族中表千人，兄弟群從且三百，何可與覆族事？

translations.literal: Shenyou's clansmen and cousins number a thousand; brothers and collateral kin nearly three hundred—how can I join in an affair that would exterminate my clan?
translations.idiomatic: My clansmen and cousins number a thousand; my brothers and extended kin nearly three hundred—how can I join in an enterprise that would exterminate my entire clan?

sentences.zh: 雖死不承命。」

translations.literal: Though I die I will not accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than accept such a command."

sentences.zh: 士良等默然，久乃啟後戶，引至小殿，帝在焉。

translations.literal: Shiliang and the others fell silent; after a long while they opened the rear door and led him to a small hall—the Emperor was there.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and the others fell silent. After a long while they opened a rear door and led him to a small hall—the Emperor was there.

sentences.zh: 士良等歷階數帝過失，帝俯首。

translations.literal: Shiliang and the others ascended the steps one by one recounting the Emperor's faults; the Emperor bowed his head.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and his allies climbed the steps one by one, reciting the Emperor's failings; the Emperor bowed his head in silence.

sentences.zh: 既而士良指帝曰：「不為學士，不得更坐此。」

translations.literal: Then Shiliang pointed at the emperor and said, "Had you not been a scholar, you would not sit here again.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shiliang pointed at the emperor and said, "Had you not been a scholar, you would never sit here again."

sentences.zh: 乃送慎由出，戒曰：「毋泄，禍及爾宗。」

translations.literal: He then sent Shenyou out, warning him, "Do not disclose this, or disaster will reach your clan."
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Shenyou out with a warning: "Tell no one, or your whole clan will suffer."

sentences.zh: 慎由記其事，藏箱枕間，時人莫知。

translations.literal: Shenyou recorded the affair and hid it between chest and pillow; at the time no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou wrote down what had happened and hid the account in a chest by his pillow. No one knew at the time.

sentences.zh: 將沒，以授其子胤，故胤惡中官，終討除之，蓋禍原於士良、弘誌雲。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he gave it to his son Yin; hence Yin hated palace eunuchs and in the end campaigned to destroy them—the origin of the disaster lay with Shiliang and Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he gave it to his son Yin. Yin came to hate palace eunuchs and in the end destroyed them—the roots of that disaster lay with Shiliang and Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 楊復光，閩人也，本喬氏。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang was a man of Min; his original surname was Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang came from Min. His birth surname was Qiao.

sentences.zh: 有武力，少養於內常侍楊玄價家，頗以節誼自奮，玄價奇之。

translations.literal: He had martial prowess and was raised in youth in the household of the inner vice attendant Yang Xuanjia; he took pride in integrity and loyalty, and Xuanjia regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was strong in arms and was raised in the household of inner vice attendant Yang Xuanjia. He prided himself on integrity and loyalty, and Xuanjia thought him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，玄價監鹽州軍，誣殺刺史劉臯。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanzong's time Xuanjia supervised the Yanzhou army and on false charges executed Prefect Liu Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong, Xuanjia supervised the Yanzhou army and on false charges executed Prefect Liu Gao.

sentences.zh: 臯有威名者，世訟其冤。

translations.literal: Gao had enjoyed a formidable reputation, and for generations his wrong was disputed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had enjoyed a formidable reputation, and for generations men disputed his wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 稍遷左神策軍中尉，譖去宰相楊收，權寵震時。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Left Shence Army Central Commander, slandered away Chief Minister Yang Shou, and his power and favor shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Shence Army Central Commander, slandered Chief Minister Yang Shou from office, and his power and favor dominated the age.

sentences.zh: 復光有謀略，累監諸鎮軍。

translations.literal: Fuguang had strategic ability and repeatedly supervised armies of various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang was strategically gifted and repeatedly supervised armies across the circuits.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，佐平盧節度使曾元裕擊賊王仙芝，敗之。

translations.literal: Early in Qianfu he assisted Pinglu military commissioner Zeng Yuanyu in attacking the bandit Wang Xianzhi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianfu he assisted Pinglu military commissioner Zeng Yuanyu against the rebel Wang Xianzhi and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 招討使宋威擊仙芝於江西，復光在軍，請判官吳彥宏約賊降，仙芝遣將尚君長自縛如約。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Song Wei attacked Xianzhi in Jiangxi; Fuguang was in the army and had his aide Wu Yanhong arrange the rebels' surrender. Xianzhi sent his general Shang Junchang bound according to the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Song Wei attacked Xianzhi in Jiangxi. Fuguang was with the army and had aide Wu Yanhong negotiate surrender. Xianzhi sent his general Shang Junchang bound, as agreed.

sentences.zh: 威疾其功，密請僖宗誅之，故仙芝怨，復引兵叛。

translations.literal: Wei resented his merit and secretly asked Emperor Xizong to execute him; hence Xianzhi bore a grudge and again raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wei resented his success and secretly asked Emperor Xizong to execute the surrender party. Xianzhi nursed a grudge and rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 後天子寤威階禍，罷之，以兵與復光，乃進禽徐唐莒。

translations.literal: Later the Son of Heaven realized Wei had escalated the disaster, removed him, and gave the troops to Fuguang, who then advanced and captured Xu, Tang, and Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later saw that Wei had worsened the disaster, removed him, and gave the troops to Fuguang, who then captured Xu, Tang, and Ju.

sentences.zh: 王鐸為招討，復光仍監軍。

translations.literal: Wang Duo served as pacification commissioner; Fuguang continued as army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo became pacification commissioner; Fuguang continued as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 鐸之棄荊南也，山南東道節度使劉巨容定其地，以忠武別將宋浩領荊南，泰寧將段彥謨佐之。

translations.literal: When Duo abandoned Jingnan, Shannan East Circuit military commissioner Liu Jurong secured the region, appointing Zhongwu deputy general Song Hao to lead Jingnan with Taining general Duan Yanmo as his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo abandoned Jingnan, Shannan East military commissioner Liu Jurong secured the region, putting Zhongwu deputy general Song Hao in charge of Jingnan with Taining general Duan Yanmo to assist him.

sentences.zh: 復光父嘗監忠武軍，而浩已為大將，見復光，少之，不為禮，彥謨亦恥居浩下，遂有隙。

translations.literal: Fuguang's father had once supervised the Zhongwu army, yet Hao was already a senior general; seeing Fuguang, he looked down on him and showed no courtesy. Yanmo also felt shame at ranking below Hao, and thus enmity arose.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang's father had once supervised the Zhongwu army, but Hao was already a senior general. He looked down on Fuguang and showed no courtesy. Yanmo was ashamed to rank below Hao, and bad blood grew between them.

sentences.zh: 復光曰：「胡不殺之？」

translations.literal: Fuguang said, "Why not kill him?
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang said, "Why not kill him?"

sentences.zh: 彥謨引慓士擊殺浩，復光以客常滋假留後，而奏浩罪，薦彥謨為朗州刺史。

translations.literal: Yanmo led fierce soldiers to strike and kill Hao. Fuguang had his client Chang Zi act as acting regent and memorialized Hao's crimes, recommending Yanmo as prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmo led fierce soldiers to kill Hao. Fuguang had his client Chang Zi serve as acting regent, memorialized Hao's crimes, and recommended Yanmo as prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔鄭紹業為荊南節度使，以復光監忠武軍，屯鄧州，遏賊右沖。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zheng Shaoye Jingnan military commissioner; Fuguang was to supervise the Zhongwu army, encamped at Dengzhou to block the rebels' right thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shaoye was appointed Jingnan military commissioner. Fuguang supervised the Zhongwu army, encamped at Dengzhou to block the rebels' right flank.

sentences.zh: 帝西幸，召紹業見行在，復光更引彥謨為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor traveled west; Shaoye was summoned to the traveling court. Fuguang again had Yanmo appointed Jingnan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled west and summoned Shaoye to the traveling court. Fuguang again installed Yanmo as Jingnan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 彥謨紿行邊，詣復光，以黃金數百兩為謝。

translations.literal: Yanmo pretended to tour the frontier, visited Fuguang, and presented several hundred taels of gold in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmo pretended to tour the frontier, visited Fuguang, and gave him several hundred taels of gold in thanks.

sentences.zh: 其後忠武周岌受賊命，嘗夜宴，召復光，左右曰：「彼既附賊，必不利公，不如毋行。」

translations.literal: Later Zhongwu's Zhou Ji accepted the rebels' commission. Once at a night banquet he summoned Fuguang; those at his side said, "He has already joined the rebels and will surely harm you—better not go.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Ji of Zhongwu accepted the rebels' commission. At a night banquet he summoned Fuguang. Attendants said, "He has joined the rebels and will surely harm you—you had better not go."

sentences.zh: 復光固往，酒所語時事，復光泣曰：「丈夫所感，獨恩與義耳，彼不顧恩義，規利害，何丈夫哉！

translations.literal: Fuguang insisted on going. Over wine they spoke of current affairs. Fuguang wept and said, "What moves a man is only grace and righteousness. He disregards grace and righteousness and schemes for profit and harm—what kind of man is that!
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang went anyway. Over wine they discussed affairs of state. Fuguang wept and said, "A man is moved only by grace and righteousness. To disregard both and scheme for profit—what kind of man is that!

sentences.zh: 公奮匹夫封侯，乃捐十八葉天子，北面臣賊，何恩義利害昧昧耶？」

translations.literal: You rose from commoner to enfeoffed lord, yet cast aside an emperor of eighteen generations to face north and serve rebels—how muddled are your notions of grace, righteousness, profit, and harm!"
translations.idiomatic: You rose from commoner to enfeoffed lord, yet cast aside an emperor of eighteen generations to bow north and serve rebels—how blind you are to grace, righteousness, profit, and harm!"

sentences.zh: 岌流涕曰：「吾力不足，陽合而陰離之，故召公計。」

translations.literal: Ji wept and said, "My strength is insufficient; I joined them outwardly while separating inwardly—therefore I summoned you to plan."
translations.idiomatic: Ji wept and said, "My strength is insufficient. I joined them in appearance while breaking away in secret—that is why I summoned you to plan."

sentences.zh: 因持杯盟曰：「有如酒！」

translations.literal: He then raised his cup in oath and said, "As this wine witnesses!"
translations.idiomatic: He raised his cup in oath: "As this wine is witness!"

sentences.zh: 即遣子守亮斬賊使於傳舍。

translations.literal: He immediately sent his son Shouliang to behead the rebel envoy at the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent his son Shouliang to behead the rebel envoy at the relay station.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權據蔡州叛，岌、復光以忠武兵三千入見之。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan seized Caizhou and rebelled; Ji and Fuguang entered to see him with three thousand Zhongwu troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan seized Caizhou and rebelled. Ji and Fuguang went to see him with three thousand Zhongwu troops.

sentences.zh: 宗權即遣部將王淑持兵萬人從。

translations.literal: Zongquan then sent his subordinate general Wang Shu with ten thousand troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan then sent his general Wang Shu with ten thousand men to follow them.

sentences.zh: 復光定荊、襄，師次鄧，淑逗遛，復光斬之，並其軍為八，以鹿宴弘、晉暉、張造、李師泰、王建、韓建等為之將，進攻南陽。

translations.literal: Fuguang secured Jing and Xiang; the army halted at Deng. Shu lingered; Fuguang beheaded him, merged his army into eight divisions, and appointed Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Zhang Zao, Li Shitai, Wang Jian, Han Jian, and others as their commanders, then advanced to attack Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang secured Jing and Xiang and halted at Deng. Shu dawdled; Fuguang executed him, reorganized his troops into eight divisions under Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Zhang Zao, Li Shitai, Wang Jian, Han Jian, and others, and advanced on Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 賊將朱溫、何勤逆戰，大敗，遂收鄧州，追北藍橋。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Zhu Wen and He Qin met them in battle and were utterly defeated; he then recovered Dengzhou and pursued north to Lanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Zhu Wen and He Qin met them in battle and were crushed. He recovered Dengzhou and pursued north to Lanqiao.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，班師。

translations.literal: When his mother died he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 俄起為天下兵馬都監，總諸軍，與東面招討使王重榮並力定關中。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Overseer of All Armies and Horses, commanding the forces jointly with Eastern Pacification Commissioner Wang Chongrong to settle Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as Overseer of All Armies and Horses, commanding the forces with Eastern Pacification Commissioner Wang Chongrong to pacify Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 朱溫守同州，復光遣使鐫諭，溫以所部降。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen held Tongzhou; Fuguang sent envoys to persuade him, and Wen surrendered with his command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen held Tongzhou. Fuguang sent envoys to win him over, and Wen surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 方賊之強，重榮憂不知所出，謂復光曰：「臣賊邪，且負國；

translations.literal: While the rebels were strong, Chongrong worried with no way out and said to Fuguang, "Am I a rebel, and have I betrayed the state?
translations.idiomatic: While the rebels were strong, Chongrong was at a loss and said to Fuguang, "Am I a rebel? Have I betrayed the state?

sentences.zh: 拒戰邪，則兵寡，柰何？」

translations.literal: If I resist in battle, my troops are few—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: If I fight, my troops are too few—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 復光曰：「李克用與我世共患難，其為人，奮不顧身，比數召未即至者，由太原道不通耳，非忍禍者。

translations.literal: Fuguang said, "Li Keyong and I have shared hardship for generations. As a man he throws himself forward without regard for his life. The reason he has not come at once though summoned several times is simply that the road from Taiyuan is blocked—not that he would endure disaster idly.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang said, "Li Keyong and I have shared hardship for generations. He is a man who throws himself forward without regard for his life. He has not come at once only because the road from Taiyuan is blocked—not because he would stand by while disaster spreads.

sentences.zh: 若諭上意，彼宜必來。」

translations.literal: If we convey the emperor's intent, he is sure to come."
translations.idiomatic: If we convey the emperor's intent, he is sure to come."

sentences.zh: 重榮曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Chongrong said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 白王鐸以詔使至太原，克用兵乃出。

translations.literal: He informed Wang Duo, and an imperial envoy was sent to Taiyuan; Keyong then led his army out.
translations.idiomatic: He informed Wang Duo, an imperial envoy was sent to Taiyuan, and Keyong led his army out.

sentences.zh: 京師平，以功加開府儀同三司、同華制置使，封弘農郡公，賜號「資忠輝武匡國平難功臣」。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, for his merit he was advanced to Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, made Tonghua Disposal Commissioner, enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Supports Loyalty, Shines in Arms, Stabilizes the State, and Pacifies Disaster."
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was pacified, for his merit he was made Grand Preceptor with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Tonghua Disposal Commissioner, and Duke of Hongnong, with the title "Meritorious Minister Who Supports Loyalty, Shines in Arms, Stabilizes the State, and Pacifies Disaster."

sentences.zh: 卒河中，贈觀軍容使，謚曰忠肅。

translations.literal: He died at Hezhong and was posthumously made Army-Supervising Commissioner, with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Hezhong and was posthumously made Army-Supervising Commissioner, with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 復光禦下有恩，軍中聞其死，皆慟哭，而麾下多立功者。

translations.literal: Fuguang treated those under him with grace; when the army heard of his death, all wept in grief, and many among his followers achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang treated his men with kindness. When the army heard of his death, all wept, and many of his followers went on to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 諸子為將帥數十人，守宗亦為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: His sons became generals and commanders by the dozens; Shouzong also served as Zhongwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of his sons became generals and commanders; Shouzong also served as Zhongwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：楚鄖公辛不敢讎君而忘父冤，昭湣之世，兩軍寵遇有厚薄，而卒用存亮夷難，功莫及者。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Duke Xin of Yun in Chu did not dare avenge his lord while forgetting his father's wrong; in the age of Zhao and Min, the two armies received favor in unequal measure, yet in the end Cunliang was used to quell disaster, and his achievement had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Duke Xin of Yun in Chu would not avenge his lord while forgetting his father's wrong. In the Zhao and Min reigns the two armies were favored unequally, yet in the end Cunliang was used to quell disaster, and none matched his achievement.

sentences.zh: 自古忠臣出於疏斥不用蓋多矣，存亮豈通記書道理之人邪，何其識君臣大誼明甚？

translations.literal: From antiquity loyal ministers have often come from those estranged and unused—was Cunliang a man versed in the records and principles of the classics? How clearly he understood the great bond between ruler and minister!
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers have often risen from those estranged and unused. Was Cunliang a man steeped in the classics? Yet how clearly he grasped the great bond between ruler and minister!

sentences.zh: 不屍大勞，畏權處外，又愈賢矣。

translations.literal: He did not cling to great merit, feared power and kept to the outer court—he was all the more worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He did not cling to great merit and, fearing power, kept to the outer court—making him all the more worthy.

sentences.zh: 與夫書「龍蛇」之詩者，何其小哉！

translations.literal: Compared with those who wrote the poem of "dragons and serpents," how petty they were!
translations.idiomatic: Beside those who wrote the poem of "dragons and serpents," how petty they seem!
